This is a problem I always encounter when I drive on a highway. The speed limit in the most used highway where I live is 70. I usually go at least 80 if not more than that, because the state is extremely beautiful and there are so many good things to see and do. I get frustrated enough driving at that speed limit as it is (70 mph) for general safety reasons but never while going over that mark. Why? Because of this: When you exceed your speed limit, your car's engine revs faster, which means that air begins to flow into the intake manifold, causing more exhaust gas to be produced. This causes an increase in power and torque, making your car accelerate rapidly, which can result in you losing control or being caught by a tractor trailer. It seems like an obvious reason why a driver would want to maintain their speed limit until they reach it! But no one does! Now, let me ask this question... Why don't people who go too fast to travel at 70mph use cruise control instead of speeding up? Here comes my point! I believe that many drivers think they have better control with cruise control and do not realize how much damage it could cause them if they were to lose control suddenly. Cruise control uses a computer to constantly monitor what speed you're traveling at and adjusts it to keep it within specified limits. If you allow the computer to adjust itself rather than using the hand controls on the steering wheel, then you risk compromising your own reaction time and possibly losing control of the vehicle altogether! (Although, accidents due to this type of condition are rare, nonetheless). So now back to my original question about why we don't speed on highways above the speed limit. Fortunately, I started my answer with the reason why we shouldn't even do that. I've got some great tips from other sources below that will hopefully help you avoid getting caught if you do happen to speed past the posted speed limit andor exceed its maximum capability.

A company based in Aberdeenshire announced that there was an "unprecedented response" to its Equity for Punks USA crowdfunding campaign. BrewDog aims to raise up to £50 million within six months to support expansion in North America. The plan includes establishing a new 100,000 square foot brewery in Columbus, Ohio, which is expected to open later this year. The shares in the funding round cost £47.50 each, with a minimum investment of £95. According to BrewDog, over 1,200 people have already registered for the scheme. On its website, the company stated, "This unprecedented response to our first crowdfunding round in the United States demonstrates the strong demand for our beer in America, and it has helped us build a community of like-minded individuals eager to assist in making our U.S. business a successful one." The Equity for Punks USA investment scheme is the fifth fundraising effort by the brewery and its first in the U.S. The Ellon-based company has raised over £26 million since launching its first Equity for Punks crowdfunding round in 2009. Its previous UK round raised £19 million to fund growth initiatives, such as expanding its brewery in Ellon and opening new bars. The round, which closed in April, did not meet its £25 million target. BrewDog's British business currently employs over 600 people worldwide and exports to 55 countries. It also operates more than 40 bars in the UK and abroad.

A database management system (DBMS) is a computer software application that interacts with users, other programs, and the database to collect and process data. A general-purpose DBMS enables the definition, construction, retrieval, modification, and control of databases. Notable DBMSs include MySQL, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, Sybase, SAP HANA, and IBM DB2. Databases are typically not easily transferable between different DBMSs, but various DBMSs can collaborate through standardized languages like SQL and ODBC or JDBC to enable a single application to function with multiple DBMSs. DBMSs are usually categorized based on the type of database model they support; the most widely used since the 1980s have all implemented the relational model via SQL. [Disputed - discussion] Occasionally, a DBMS is simply called a "database."

My phone buzzed for the fourth time that day, and I scrambled to check it, desperately hoping it was a call back from that job I'd applied for. My current job wasn't cutting it, and money was running thin. This editing job wasn't the dream, but if I got the position I'd be able to at least live comfortably. No, it wasn't. It was just an e-mail notification, another of those damned spams asking me to "JOIN THE ILLUMANITI TODAY! WE NEED YOU." Jesus fuck, that had to be the thousandth I'd received in the past month alone, and it had been going on for a long time. No matter what I did to block them, the e-mails returned. Add them to the spam filter? They started coming from other e-mail addresses for the next day, and then the day after that they were back from the first. Block them with another app or adblock? They still showed up. I'd even deleted my e-mail app, but lo and behold, e-mail notifications started coming through other places. Facebook, YouTube, and I even started getting inbox messages on Reddit. I didn't think much of it beyond some asshole pulling an over-the-top prank. There was a fiction writing website that I liked to participate on regularly, and I spent most of my time in the science-fiction section, writing collaborative dystopia stories with a friend. I was always the one to structure those dystopian societies and everything they did. We had a lot of fun, and readers gave us some pretty good reviews. I didn't foresee any negative consequences. The e-mails started when we wrote about a world in which the Illuminati ruled everything. So obviously, I ignored them, figuring that it was my friend pranking me. But as the e-mails kept coming, I asked him, and it was clear he had no idea what I was talking about. So it wasn't him, but it could have easily been someone else from that site. This notification had come through Facebook, so I decided to go ahead and delete that from my phone. It was getting annoying as hell. I'd scarcely finished dragging the app over to the little trash can when the phone began vibrating and buzzing excitedly while the phone call notification bar appeared at the top. Finally, what I'd been waiting for all along! My struggles could be forgotten at last with this job. Forgetting my annoyance, I rushed to press the answer button and held it up to my face, eagerly saying, " Hello? " " Hello, Tom. " A gravelly voice responded from the other end, causing me to frown. This wasn't the voice of the woman who had interviewed me. " Uh, hi? May I ask who I'm speaking with? " I asked my question quickly, desperate to get the call over with as soon as possible. I didn't want to miss that call. It wouldn't look good on me. " Tom, you've been ignoring us for quite a long time. I don't think you understand how serious our offer is. We have waited for long enough. The Illumaniti is your future. We are your only path forward in life. " I sighed in annoyance. " Jesus Christ, dude, knock it the fuck off! I am sick of this stupid joke of yours. Don't you know when something's gone on long enough? Now if you'll excuse me, I'm going to hang up. I'm waiting for a call back. " I was taking the phone away to end the call, but the sound of his laughter stopped me. It was slow and halting, and I honestly could not tell if it was fake or sincere. " Tom, you won't be getting a call from Melissa. Not anytime soon, and not ever. We have told her not to give you the job. And, don't worry about hanging up. I will do it for you. We are waiting outside your apartment. " The call ended abruptly, and there was a harsh rapping at the door. A knot twisted and tied itself in my stomach, and I felt sweat trickling down my face. The last thing I wanted to do was answer it, but what could I do but open that door? Slowly, I crossed my apartment. The knocking did not stop. It was slow and persistent. Knock..... 1..... 2..... Knock..... 1..... 2..... Knock. Finally, I reached the door. I placed my hand on the knob, and hesitated. The knocking continued, and I suddenly panicked and swung it open, certain that the longer I waited, the greater the horror beyond would become. I was greeted with the sight of a slim, balding man, hardly over five and a half feet tall. He wore a suit, far fancier than anything I'd ever even seen in my lifetime, with a neat black tie that pointed to his shining black shoes. In his hands, he carried a briefcase. A bright and cheery smile spread across his face. " Hello, Tom. " It was that same voice I'd heard on the phone. He extended his hand. In the presence of this man who simply oozed luxury and confidence, I felt very awkward standing there in a stained white t-shirt and jeans with holes that weren't meant for fashion. But it would be rude to not shake his hand, so I shrugged my shoulders and accepted. Without waiting for me to invite him, he walked into my apartment, brushing me aside without even having to touch me. He sat at my tiny, pathetic excuse for a dining room table and I dumbly followed him, giving up on making sense of the situation. I sat across from him and then stared at him, trying to discern what his intentions might be. He met my gaze steadily, his cold gray eyes meeting mine without flinching. " So, uh, are you really with the Illuminati? If, uh, it actually exists and all that? " I asked. " You know the answer to that, Tom. That is not why I am here. I am here for you. It is time for you to join us. Your vision is far grander than even you know, Tom. We want you, and you need us. " His eyes did not move, and his happy smile never left his face, but his voice remained slow and deep. It was a voice that was immediately accepted as telling the truth. " Wait, my vision? Is this, uh, about my writing? Cuz that's all fiction, you know. I'm just a writer, just a nobody. I just wan na live a normal life, writing, editing, whatever. Literature is my passion, dude. None of this secret-society or whatever you guys are. " I shook my head, confused, not able to believe what I was hearing. " There is no future for you outside of us. We have made sure of it. Do not worry, Tom. You won't have to stop writing. You will be able to write as much as you want. Is there nothing grander for a writer than to see his vision come to life? Not in a cheap movie that misses the point, but in the whole of society? You will live well, Tom. Above the rich, above the politicians. Above even me. " His smile broadened at that, and he flashed his pure white teeth at me. Then, he opened the briefcase. I looked inside and saw the money. My breath left me all at once. " You know what? You've got yourself a deal. "

Officials plan to raise the maximum discount, currently set at PS16,000, to over PS50,000. They aim to encourage more renters and lenders to participate in the initiative, which began in the 1980s. However, a housing organization, Shelter, warns that this approach might reduce the availability of "realistically affordable" social housing. It also raises concerns about placing additional financial strain on low-income households through potential mortgage debt. The "right to buy" program was initiated during Margaret Thatcher's tenure. In December, the government announced a consultation on revitalizing the scheme, proposing a maximum discount of PS50,000. Current discount levels vary nationwide, from PS16,000 to PS38,000. Ministers now advocate for discounts exceeding PS75,000, according to the BBC. The government claims that all sold social homes will be replaced by new affordable rent properties, maintaining the number of affordable homes. Shelter, however, argues this strategy may still harm social housing. Roger Harding, Shelter’s head of policy, noted that the government does not replace like-with-like. The "affordable rent" model allows landlords to charge up to 80% of market rates, often higher than council rates. This results in fewer genuinely affordable homes for low-income families. Harding further stated that this could increase housing benefits if there are fewer council houses and more "affordable rent" properties with higher costs. He also highlighted concerns that ownership may not always be the best option for social housing tenants, many of whom face financial difficulties with mortgage payments. Statistically, the right-to-buy scheme has seen declining participation.

The British failures in North America, combined with other failures in the European theater, led to the fall from power of Newcastle and his principal military advisor, the Duke of Marlborough. Although he continued to lead the British army in France, Marlborough's personal popularity plummeted and he was replaced as Prime Minister by Lord Shelburne. The naval failure in the West Indies in the war's opening months was the last straw. Newcastle was recalled to England and the government, which had been a minority Whig administration, became a Whig-dominated coalition under Shelburne. Shelburne's coalition proved unable to address the many problems facing Britain in the American War of Independence. Despite British success in the early stages of the war, the coalition government began to back away from fighting a long war. It sought to make peace with the colonists in 1775, but the American war continued for several years longer. The American war was not just about military victory, but also about the nation's future. The American War of Independence was the first time that the vast majority of British subjects who lived outside the British Empire engaged in a national struggle against the mother country. The American colonists saw the war as a rebellion against the British Empire. The colonies sought to make their own decisions about their future and to be free of British control. Although many colonists felt that the colonies had been abused by the British government, the war was not fought to punish the colonists. The war was fought to defend British values and to restore the authority of the monarchy. After Britain's defeat in the American War of Independence, it began to reorganize itself. In 1783, it created the British North America Act, which separated the British colonies from the British mainland and established the province of Quebec. Although it lost the colonies in North America, Britain maintained its dominance in the British Isles. The British Navy dominated the seas, while the British Army was the largest in Europe. However, the British Empire, although the most powerful empire in the world, was not an empire of one nation. It was a multinational empire, which included millions of subjects who spoke many different languages. It was also an empire that was divided by religious and cultural differences. The Empire was a patchwork of different groups and peoples. Many of the empire's subjects lived in the colonies, while others lived in the British Isles. It was an empire of aristocrats, clergy, commoners, and immigrants. Many of the empire's subjects were illiterate and the empire was governed by a hierarchical, authoritarian system. The empire's population included millions of Catholics, Protestants, and Jews. The empire's subjects also included thousands of people of African descent, who were the descendants of slaves. Although the British Empire was an empire of many peoples, the British government sought to create a new type of empire. It attempted to transform the empire into a "Commonwealth of Nations," which would be a new type of government, which would be open to all of the empire's subjects. It would be an empire that was free from any racial or religious restrictions. It would be an empire in which all of the empire's subjects could have a voice in government. Although it did not succeed in its aim of creating a new type of empire, the British government did seek to reduce the empire's religious and racial divisions. It abolished the slave trade and outlawed the practice of slavery. The British government also began to allow immigrants to immigrate to the empire and to participate in the British government. The British government also sought to modernize the empire and to improve its institutions. It built new roads, railways, and bridges. It also began to build new schools, hospitals, and orphanages. However, despite these efforts, the empire remained divided by religion, race, and language. The empire was also plagued by rebellions, uprisings, and revolts. The revolt of the American colonies against the British Empire was the first major rebellion in the British Empire. The revolt of the Sepoys against the British in India in 1857 was the first major uprising in the British Empire. It was followed by the Indian Rebellion of 1858 and the Gordon Riots in England in 1801. The 1857 revolt in India led to the partition of Bengal and the creation of two new provinces in India, Bengal and Bombay. The British government also established a new administrative system for the empire, which it called the Imperial Legislative Council.

A machine learning system can achieve good performance on a specific test set by using heuristics that work effectively for common input types but falter in complex scenarios. In the context of natural language inference (NLI), which involves assessing whether one sentence logically implies another, we examine this challenge. We propose that statistical NLI models might rely on three flawed syntactic heuristics: the lexical similarity heuristic, the subsequence heuristic, and the constituent heuristic. To assess whether models employ these heuristics, we develop a controlled experiment called HANS (Heuristic Analysis for NLI Systems), which includes numerous instances where these heuristics fail. Our findings indicate that models trained on the MNLI dataset, such as BERT, perform poorly on HANS, implying they have indeed utilized these heuristics. This suggests that NLI systems have significant potential for enhancement, and the HANS dataset can serve as a tool to evaluate and drive development in this field.

When I realized that you were not here to harm me, I decided to assist you in your quest. It is the least I could do as a gesture of goodwill." The princess lowered her sword, still eyeing the dragon warily. "But why did you kidnap me in the first place?" The dragon let out a short sigh. "I apologize for that, Princess. I have since learned the error of my ways and I hope to make amends." The prince and princess exchanged a glance before turning back to the dragon. "Well, we appreciate your assistance," the prince said. "But what do we do now? Our quest was to rescue the princess, but since you're not our enemy, we don't know what to do next." Australian and European police were informed about a paedophile website known as the Love Zone, which operated within the so-called dark web. The site was secured with passwords, encryption, and specialized software, allowing users to remain completely anonymous. The content featured disturbing imagery, including the abuse of infants and young children. To maintain their presence on the site, members had to upload increasingly explicit material. There were numerous accounts on the platform. Australian officers with Task Force Argos discovered that the site's creator used the phrase "hiyas" as a greeting. After searching through public chat rooms and forums, they located a Facebook profile of a man using the same greeting. Though the profile was fabricated, it contained a photograph of a vehicle, leading them to identify a man named Shannon McCoole, a childcare worker in Adelaide. When officers arrived at his home, he was actively managing the site. They captured detailed photos of his hands, where a freckle matched one seen in several of the abusive images. Task Force Argos then assumed McCoole's identity and took control of the site. Last year, he received a 35-year prison sentence. A notable user was Huckle, who had access to numerous children and exhibited aggressive behavior. By analyzing data from the site and information Huckle shared online, officers identified him and his location. Recognizing he would return to the UK for the Christmas holidays in 2014, they alerted Britain's National Crime Agency. Upon his arrival at Gatwick Airport, officers from the NCA's Child Exploitation and Online Protection unit seized hundreds of obscene images and videos from his computer and encrypted storage devices.

An identity refers to the role that an individual or group assumes within highly specialized modern societies. This study aims to categorize Twitter users according to their role identities. Initially, we gather a broad-based public figure dataset through automatic means, followed by manual labeling of a more detailed identity set. We introduce a hierarchical self-attention neural network for classifying Twitter user roles. Experimental results show that the proposed method surpasses several baseline models. Additionally, we suggest a transfer learning approach that enhances model performance substantially and significantly decreases the requirement for extensive human-labeled data.

We focus on determining dense subsets of multivariate Gaussian random variables within a graphical model context. We introduce two new estimators grounded in the Ordered Weighted 1 (OWL) norm: 1) The Graphical OWL (GOWL) employs the OWL norm on the lower triangular elements of the precision matrix. 2) The column-by-column Graphical OWL (ccGOWL) uses OWL-regularized linear regression to estimate the precision matrix. Both approaches effectively detect strongly correlated variable groups while maintaining sparsity in the estimated precision matrix. We construct GOWL as a composite optimization problem and demonstrate its unique global solution. Additionally, we derive sufficient grouping criteria for each column of the ccGOWL precision matrix. Proximal descent algorithms are proposed to optimize both estimators. For datasets with group structures, the ccGOWL estimator exhibits substantial computational savings and matches or exceeds existing methods in accuracy. Computational timing results confirm the ccGOWL's efficiency. We apply the ccGOWL method to cancer gene expression and equity data sets to evaluate its grouping performance.

Automated hyperparameter optimization (HPO) has shown great power in many machine learning applications. While existing methods suffer from model selection, parallelism, or sample efficiency, this paper presents a new HPO method, MOdular FActorial Design (MOFA), to address these issues simultaneously. The major idea is to use techniques from Experimental Designs to improve sample efficiency of model-free methods. Particularly, MOFA runs with four modules in each iteration: (1) an Orthogonal Latin Hypercube (OLH) -based sampler preserving both univariate projection uniformity and orthogonality; (2) a highly parallelized evaluator; (3) a transformer to collapse the OLH performance table into a specified Fractional Factorial Design-Orthogonal Array (OA); (4) an analyzer including Factorial Performance Analysis and Factorial Importance Analysis to narrow down the search space. We theoretically and empirically show that MOFA has great advantages over existing model-based and model-free methods.

Maximilien de Robespierre was a man of great convictions and great intentions. I still remember the whispered praises of French men and women on their death beds. With but a few remaining mortal breaths they reveled in the hope that'The Incorruptible' had given their lives. No man was more of a hero of the people than he. During this time I admit shame, for I yearned to visit France and discover what new battles he waged. The equality of vote brought him deserved renown. His opposition to slavery displayed chivalry. When he turned to abolish the death penalty I could only feel admiration. That may seem odd to you, but it was originally death by natural cause that gave my birth my predecessors and I. Death by man is an abomination, and I cheered for his cause from the shadows. At some point, a gray haired, ill-groomed man called me as he clutched at his heart amidst a crowd gathered for Robespierre. The Incorruptible's eloquent speech energized my soul in a way no mortal had done before. And so it was through others' misfortune, through eavesdropping in on the final conversations of French lives that I gradually witnessed Robespierre's corruption of spirit. Some say power perverted his integrity. Others believe he simply sacrificed for a greater good. But the dying have no need to lie, and so I can say with certainty that neither party was wrong. So dedicated to his cause, he fully relinquished his moral compass. He rescinded his opposition to the death penalty and executed former friends and allies as readily as Louis XVI. Tens of thousands died by his direction. He demanded citizens be given democracy, but could not abide those who would not embrace their despot's views. From time to time, I can still hear the guillotine working tirelessly to still the surviving opposition in Vendee. Heads filled baskets meant for flowers and fruit. But it was a final pair of brown eyes I would remember best. Robespierre's lifeless stare showed regret, but I know not if for his failures to realize his dream or for the cruelty he enacted to achieve it. After, as has been done many times before and will be done many times after, death took a new face. My retired colleagues thought me brave to handle such massacre. My retired colleagues thought me resolute to see the Reign of Terror to its end. My retired colleagues thought me foolish when I predicted these deaths would be a blip on the radar of human persecution. I admit it was a horrific time, but I am only glad my calling came when it did and not a century and a half later. Nightmares still haunt Tomas in a manner that no angel deserves. And the worst is still yet to come.

David reviewed all his choices once more, constantly shifting locations. "I could go back. I could check what's at the end," he thought as he stepped into the dining room. "I'm not lying; I'm curious. Time doesn't change here, but I feel like I've been on the run for at least a month. I don't want all that running to be pointless," he muttered as he entered the living room for the twenty-fifth time that day and sank onto the couch, taking a deep breath. "I know there's an end. I know there is. Last time I was in the kitchen, I saw myself and he told me there was an end. He hadn't seen it, but he had been told so. I was told to turn back, that it wasn't worth it. As he left the room, I stopped him to ask how long he'd been running for. He said he didn't know." David stood up, cautious not to stay too long lest the person following him get closer. He went to the door leading to the hallway, opened it, and took a step into the mostly empty guest room. "None of this makes any sense," he realized as he considered the creature following him. It was a human, mostly. It seemed like an alien who had never seen a human before had been given a description of one and asked to draw it. It was roughly shaped like a human, but things weren't always in the right place. The knees bent incorrectly, the hands were too small and misshaped, and his face... oh god, his face... David shivered and opened the closet door, returning to the living room for the twenty-sixth time that day.

It's mostly a matter of training. Yes, some people are born with perfect pitch. A lot of the time, though, you can be trained to play something by ear. The first part of playing by ear is pitch identification. This is normally a crapshoot, but if you're sitting at a keyboard you can identify it by approximating the pitch in your head, then double-checking by playing along with the actual song. However, some people are born with intrinsic pitch identification abilities. The second part is interval identification.'Interval' means the space between two notes. This is easier than pitch because you can identify the intervals and play, even if it's in the wrong key. As I said, a lot of this comes down to training even though some people can just naturally do it.

Kyra looked down at the metal box she held in her hands, and couldn't help but feel disappointed. She struggled to keep her face neutral as she disentangled herself from the brightly coloured pink wrapping paper that the box had come wrapped in. The card didn't even have money in. "Thanks Uncle Rufus," she said, finally looking up. Kyra schooled her features into polite happiness and grinned at Uncle Rufus, who sat in the rocking chair by the window. Mother didn't like him much, because he refused to remove his muddy boots when he came into their house, and the tartan shirt he wore stunk of pipe-smoke and peat. He still had dirt beneath his fingernails and his red hair was tousled by the wind, beard straggly as a bird's nest. "I really like the present." She placed her hand inside the box and nudged at the small, scaled creature that was coiled inside. It was smaller than a mouse, tiny combs like a cockerel's lining the back of its neck and down to the tiny tail, no wider than a needle at its base. At her touch, the dragon stirred itself and turned towards her hand. Its eyes were blue as sapphires, flashing against the deep royal green of the scales on its face. Two stubs on its back were all that promised the advent of wings. "They grow," Uncle Rufus promised. "That's a Scotch dragon. One of the last. I found the mother myself, after she'd birthed six of'em in a little bothy on my land. Almost burnt myself getting it away from her! Tha' was the smallest, thought it'd be perfect for little Kyra here." The last bit was addressed to Kyra's mother, who frowned. "I'm not sure it's entirely appropriate for a child," she said. Her mouth had become a hard, flat line. Meanwhile, the dragon had nestled against the palm of Kyra's hand, closing its eyes and snuffling quietly. She had wanted a Pets Hospital, but as the dragon's warmth began to blaze against her palm, she realised she didn't mind too much. "I like it, Mum," she said. "It's alright, can I keep it?" A moment of hesitation. "Pleaseeee," she whined. "She can come up to Jura with me if she wants," Uncle Rufus said. He was her dad's brother, not her mum's, and her dad was long gone. Kyra had only ever heard stories about the Scotch highlands, the dragons that walked the land: the size of cats, cars and castles. "Over the summer holidays. She needs to get out of London, the air's no good for her round here, with all those cars and busses." "You can keep the dragon," Mum relented. She didn't look happy about it. "We'll talk about Scotland later." She picked up Uncle Rufus' mug, frown still etched tight on her face, and swept from the room. Kyra lifted the little green dragon from the box and looked at her Uncle. He stared intently as the dragon scurried up Kyra's arm like a mouse, the claws like small pinpricks on her skin. "You got a name for her, lass?" He asked. "It always starts with a name." rSchoolgirlerror

Firstly, certain costs are difficult to avoid and are shared by everyone, such as the costs of housing, pensions, education and health care. If the state does not provide these these services for all citizens then developing an independent national free-market system will be far more politically expedient. This is a dangerous idea given that in most countries there has been no single government in Europe or Asia to completely control the economy and social growth. The European Union should continue its role as a global economic powerhouse with a central bank capable of making decisions on behalf of people at home without affecting the economy. The EU alone can create 200 jobs and contribute about 1 trillion annually to developmentally vulnerable nations and communities. It needs to support attempts to reduce inequality. In many ways, this would make it possible to have everything we need to develop the world's fastest growing economies and raise living standards above average across most developed societies around the globe from now until 2035. The UK should also follow suit. Governments must pursue reforms based on the principle of free markets in which every citizen's right to vote affects their lives. In the US, new legislation must be introduced and enacted to promote open markets, post-election alliances between democratic governments and nonvoters, and strengthen anti-trust laws and protections against unfair trade practices. Some reform proposals should include greater transparency regarding the size of public investment for public good; set up the independence of national institutions and the creation of independent commissions to launch investigations into alleged bribery and corruption; take away from parliament power some complex processes required for judicial oversight and ensure that every person can hold to account those who invest in contravention of Romanian law or immigration rules. This will encourage countries to adopt better democratic procedures to defend their rights under international treaties and obligations. Countries should also demand that the United Nations temporarily suspend the accession process until the negotiations have concluded. Parties should also pledge to implement safeguards to protect the integrity of countries' elections made available through negotiation. EU member states should assume responsibility for reopening the door to the further expansion of democracy. It should be clear that international governance requires governing principles that respect the freedoms of expression and comments. Freedom of speech encourages openness and is guaranteed by Lisbon's Convention on Human Rights (CRH), where freedom of expression is enshrined in section 36 of the Constitution. Underwater imagery has enabled numerous civilian applications in various domains, ranging from academia to industry, and from industrial surveillance and maintenance to environmental protection and behavior of marine creatures studies. In the academic domain, underwater imagery has been used for oceanography research, geology and sediment studies, marine biology and ecology surveys, archaeological research, and technology development. In industry, underwater imaging is used for applications such as pipeline inspections, oil rig inspections, shipwreck searches, and other underwater salvage operations. Underwater imagery can also be used for commercial purposes such as underwater photography and videography, marine engineering or construction projects, recreational activities such as fishing and scuba diving, and navigation. Additionally, underwater imagery has proven to be a valuable tool in environmental protection as well. It can be used to monitor coral reefs, track algae growth and its effects on aquatic ecosystems, assess the effects of pollution and overfishing, and detect invasive species. Finally, underwater imagery has been used to study the behavior of marine creatures, such as whales, sharks, and dolphins, as well as understanding their migratory patterns and habits.

This is the news title today: Up to 70 of people in developed countries 'have seen incomes stagnate' But at the same time, the following this are observed: "Incomes are rising fastest for the richest" "People in developed countries are becoming richer at a faster pace than in developing countries" "Incomes in the US have grown at almost twice the global average since 2008" "The richest 1 of US households have seen their incomes soar by nearly 150 since 1999" So how do we reconcile these two contradicting points? We are told that the income of the richest in the US has soared by nearly 150 and yet up to 70 of the people in the US and the developed countries have seen their incomes stagnate. If we average out the income growth rate of the 70 of the people that have seen their incomes stagnate, it works out to about 0.5 per year. But the income growth rate of the richest 1 is nearly 3 times that. So the rich are getting richer at a faster pace than the poor are getting poorer. If income inequality is a problem, then we should be measuring how much the richest are getting richer relative to the poorest getting poorer. It is only when the poor get poorer faster than the rich get richer that we can see that there is a problem. But when the rich get richer faster than the poor get poorer, it means that the problem is not income inequality but rather income stagnation. The article is conflating two different issues. The following is taken from the 2017 Federal Budget released last week. The chart on page 14 shows the income and taxation revenue. The top 1 of income earners contribute nearly 30 of the tax revenue. The bottom 50 of the income earners contribute less than 10 of the tax revenue. Now you might be thinking that it is unfair that the top 1 have to pay nearly 30 of the tax revenue while the bottom 50 have to pay less than 10 of the tax revenue. But we are told that the top 1 are getting richer and the bottom 50 are getting poorer. So how can the bottom 50 have to pay less than 10 of the tax revenue when they earn less than 20 of the total income? If the top 1 have to pay 30 of the tax revenue while earning less than 20 of the total income, then the bottom 50 must be paying more than 10 of the tax revenue. In other words, it is a mis-statement to say that the bottom 50 have to pay less than 10 of the tax revenue. They must be paying more than 10 of the tax revenue.

Towcester racecourse chief executive Kevin Ackerman has failed in his bid to overturn a six-month suspension from racing. Ackerman, who was appointed as CEO at Towcester in 2012, had his license suspended by the British Horseracing Authority (BHA) after he was found guilty of failing to provide financial information relating to the racecourse's accounts. The BHA said the suspension was necessary to ensure that any future financial dealings between the racecourse and its customers were conducted in accordance with the rules and regulations set out by the sport's governing body. Ackerman, however, argued that the suspension was unjustified and appealed the decision. However, at a hearing held on Tuesday, the court ruled in favour of the BHA and upheld the suspension. Speaking after the hearing, Ackerman said he was disappointed with the result but accepted the decision. "I have taken due account of today's decision and would like to thank everyone for their support throughout this process," he said. The BHA welcomed the ruling, saying it was pleased that its decision had been upheld. "We are pleased that the court has recognised that the integrity of our sport is paramount and that we must be able to ensure that all participants comply with the rules and regulations," a spokesperson said. The suspension will see Ackerman barred from taking part in any horseracing activities for the next six months. It also means that the Towcester racecourse will have to operate without its CEO during that period. The BHA added that they expect the racecourse to comply with all relevant regulations while Ackerman is away.

When the disease finally left my body it left it weak, my lungs wheezed with every breathe and my muscles were left thin and atrophied. If I was from a less affluent family I may have been left to die. Luckily for me, my family was not about to let their firstborn son die. They would also not allow me to show the family as weak, so I was locked away. My brother tells me that he fought for years to keep me as the heir to the family. He said that he argued until he was blue in the face that the Dracul blood was strong and that I would eventually recover. "Just give him time," he said, I would be able to take over the duties of master of the house given time. Sometimes I would show improvement, my family rejoiced and my dear brother returned from his travels abroad to help nurse me back to health once again. Unhappily my health never stayed long after the celebrations began. It was as if the mere presence of such joyful happiness poisoned my body. I would began to vomit and become bedridden again for cause of muscle spasms. Through this all my brother would nurse me, spoon feeding me his exotic medicines that he had collected on his travels late into the the night. Always hoping that one of them would finally cure me. Eventually my father had his way, my brother was to be the new head of the family. All of the Dracul land, titles, and riches were to go to him. My loving brother said that he begged father to wait just a little longer, to leave me some small smidgen of inheritance, but it was to no avail. My father died soon after naming my brother heir, before I was ever able to reconcile myself with him. With my father's death, Vladimir moved back home and began his duties as the head of house Dracul fully. Today I awoke feeling better than I had in a very long time. Perhaps I would leave my room and surprise Vlad with how my health, wouldn't he be so happy? I had not been into the upper chambers since my father had been alive and I had been being groomed for eventual lordship of our house but I still remembered the way, I still remembered the correct way to unlock the siege door. A door intended to seal away an entire wing of the castle. Should the worst happen and the castle be invaded the siege door had the ability to lock and steal away the lord of the house, preserving our family's history and the life of anyone behind it long enough for help to arrive. The torches along the walls were not lit and it didn't seem as if they had been for a long time. Regardless, I could still peer through the darkness and what I saw..... What I saw terrified me.

A effective method to assess competitiveness involves comparing the quality-to-price ratio of services against profit margins. Some businesses can be competitive even when generating massive profits, as their large-scale operations often result in profits that aren't particularly informative without considering costs and profit margins. Exxon has a 7.43 profit margin, whereas Apple boasts a 21.28 profit margin. It's been noted that the electronics sector isn't typically considered non-competitive.

The key factor lies in defining competitiveness. A straightforward test is to evaluate whether firms can dictate the market price of their products. Exxon cannot arbitrarily set the price of a gallon of gasoline at $5.00 if others are selling at $4.00; this would lead to reduced sales as consumers might opt for alternative providers. If Exxon could charge $1 more per gallon, it indicates the market is non-competitive. If Exxon could charge $1 more than competitors, it suggests Exxon holds sufficient market share so consumers have no alternatives. If Exxon controlled 50% of the market, consumers might be compelled to purchase from Exxon regardless of price.

Additionally, understanding the distinction between profit and profit margins is essential. Profit refers to total earnings minus expenses. Profit margin calculates profit relative to expenses. For instance, if a company generates $150 billion in revenue and incurs $100 billion in costs, its profit is $50 billion, and its profit margin is 50%. In 2013, Exxon earned $101 billion in revenue with $100 billion in costs, yielding $1 billion in profit but a mere 1% profit margin. Generally, the higher the profit margin, the less competitive a company is. Exxon’s 7.53 profit margin places it in the mid-range of profit margins.

However, 770,000 EU nationals living in the capital should be eligible for a visa to ensure their future in London, the chamber of commerce said. They make up 15 of London's employees. EU nationals also contribute more than PS26bn to London's Gross Value Added - the value of goods and services produced - and they pay direct taxes of about PS7bn a year. Their departure from the workforce "would be economically harmful, impacting on various key industries and putting pressure on public funds," the chamber's research suggests. It could particularly hit construction, where foreign workers make up a third of the workforce, and financial services, where they make up a quarter. In that sector there are acute worries post-Brexit about the future of passporting rights - an agreement that allows UK businesses to offer financial services anywhere in the EU and the wider European Economic Area including Norway, Iceland and and Lichtenstein, without the need for licences in individual countries. Although this has yet to be clarified by the government, it is thought EU immigrants will in future have to enter the UK under the same arrangements applicable to non-EU migrants now which imposes minimum salary levels and insists on firm job offers. Research suggests that by 2020, London may have lost access to 160,000 migrant workers, and there would be a loss to economic output of nearly PS7bn a year and direct tax contributions of about PS2bn. The report recommends: City Hall said the mayor was committed to keeping London open to foreign talent, but he is yet to commit to special immigration measures. Speaking at an event launching the report, Ben Johnson, an adviser to the mayor on business, said the ability to attract foreign workers was vital along with "privileged" access to the single market. He said the priority was to secure the future of the workers here now, although there was no explicit support from him for any of the business proposals. Greater London Authority Conservative group leader Gareth Bacon said: "Now that we have won the war over Brexit and have re-secured the power to govern ourselves, we have a great opportunity to shape our immigration policy in ways that best suit our needs and ambitions. The primary feature of the skin of an aircraft is to be just strong enough to hold up against the air (to make it aerodynamic) and as light as possible. It tends to be pretty soft and thin aluminum. The primary feature of turbine blades is strength and temperature resistance. They are both metals, but they are in completely different classes when it comes to hardness. Turbine blade strength, especially at high temperatures, is one of the primary limiting factors when it comes to modern jet engine design, and has been a key driver in the development of new ceramics and super alloys. We've moved past turbine blade materials able to withstand high-speed hail decades ago, and we still are after yet harder materials.

Laurisilva is a unique type of subtropical rainforest found in few areas of Europe and the world: in the Azores, and in particular on the island of Madeira, there are large forests of endemic Laurisilva forests (the latter protected as a natural heritage preserve). There are several species of diverse mammalian fauna, including the fox, badger, iberian lynx, iberian wolf, wild goat (Capra pyrenaica), wild cat (Felis silvestris), hare, weasel, polecat, chameleon, mongoose, civet, brown bear[citation needed] (spotted near Rio Minho, close to Peneda-Geres) and many others. Portugal is an important stopover for migratory birds, in places such as Cape St. Vincent or the Monchique mountains, where thousands of birds cross from Europe to Africa during the autumn or in the spring (return migration).

Shattered armor and sharpened weapons lay scattered around, stripped of their intended use and devoid of the promise of flesh to tear apart. A harsh wind swept across the barren battlefield, leaving only his own blood and the remains of the figure emerging from the nearby hill. Even the once-bleeding Roman, who had been cradled in Dunstan's arms just moments before, was now reduced to empty robes. Calling it an invasion would have been a cruel jest. The northern forces had vastly outnumbered the small watchtower, with many thousands to one. It wasn’t a matter of whether the tower would fall, but rather how long it might last and whether the attackers would be tormented before dying. Many were already dead. Dunstan had no alternative but to comply. "You are the one who called me then?" a voice rumbled, akin to the groaning of a trebuchet’s wheels. It wasn’t a question, merely an acknowledgment. Dunstan turned his head, bowing slightly, locking eyes with the towering figure now standing beside him. His clean, white suit bore a design the mage had never seen. A deity, one whose true name had faded into obscurity, a warrior and trader, stood over him. His face, fierce and unyielding, obscured the sunlight like a storm cloud. Dunstan nodded politely. Much of his own blood had been shed in the conflict, but compared to the countless who had perished, he couldn’t help but feel slighted. "What shall I call you?" he asked, rising to his feet. The beast-man grasped the empty robes at Dunstan’s feet, as if reading something within their threads. "You may call me Roman," he sneered. His teeth were like ivory, so sharp that even looking at them felt like a paper cut on Dunstan’s eyes. "Where is my war I was promised?" "There is none. You ended it—Roma."

Most animals obtain energy from sunlight indirectly by consuming plants or herbivores. Plants utilize sunlight to transform inorganic substances in their surroundings into carbohydrates, fats, proteins, and other organic molecules, typically featuring reduced carbon linked to hydrogen atoms. This process begins with carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water (H₂O), converting sunlight into chemical energy stored as simple sugars like glucose. The resulting sugars serve as the foundation for plant development and the creation of additional biomolecules. When animals consume plants (or other animals that have consumed plants), the carbon-based compounds in their diet provide energy and structural components necessary for the animal's growth. These compounds can be used immediately for development or decomposed, releasing stored solar energy to fuel movement and activity.

Given a positive integer k, a k -dominating set in a graph G is a set of vertices such that every vertex not in the set has at least k neighbors in the set. A total k -dominating set, also known as a k -tuple total dominating set, is a set of vertices such that every vertex of the graph has at least k neighbors in the set. The problems of finding the minimum size of a k -dominating, respectively total k -dominating set, in a given graph, are referred to as k -domination, respectively total k -domination. These generalizations of the classical domination and total domination problems are known to be NP-hard in the class of chordal graphs, and, more specifically, even in the classes of split graphs (both problems) and undirected path graphs (in the case of total k -domination). On the other hand, it follows from recent work of Kang et al. (2017) that these two families of problems are solvable in time O (V (G) 6 k 4) in the class of interval graphs. We develop faster algorithms for k -domination and total k -domination in the class of proper interval graphs, by means of reduction to a single shortest path computation in a derived directed acyclic graph with O (V (G) 2 k) nodes and O (V (G) 4 k) arcs. We show that a suitable implementation, which avoids constructing all arcs of the digraph, leads to a running time of O (V (G) 3 k). The algorithms are also applicable to the weighted case.

This implies that if a resident's care is needed while temporarily residing in the UK—whether for leisure or work—they will receive treatment, and the NHS will recover the associated costs from the respective country. Nobles were typically born into noble families, or they could be adopted by a noble family (which was abolished in 1633), or they could gain nobility through the favor of a king or the Sejm for reasons such as bravery in battle, public service, or other merits—though this was exceptionally rare. Many nobles were actually commoners who moved to different regions and falsely claimed noble status. Hundreds of these impostors were documented by Hieronim Nekanda Trepka in his work "Liber generationis plebeanorium" (or "Liber chamorum") during the early 16th century. The law prohibited non-nobles from holding noble estates, and it offered the estate to the person who denounced the imposter. Trepka, an impoverished noble living in town, gathered numerous accounts of such cases, aiming to secure estates for himself. However, he never successfully proved any of these claims before the courts. Over the centuries, several Sejms issued decrees to address the issue, but their effectiveness was limited. While it remains unclear how many members of the Polish nobility originated from lower social classes, most historians believe that nobles of humble birth constituted a significant portion of the szlachta.

I close my eyes. The nurse had marked the time of death as 15:07, but the patient on the table was not yet gone, as far as both the patient and I were concerned. A sudden aortic dissection. She is 27. Her hair is brown and her skin is still warm. My number was on her necklace next to the letters ICE: in case of emergency. I arrived at 14:30 and completed my work at 3:00 the next morning. By the time I had finished, there was no blood left. Only ice. I had met her once when she came to sign her contract for preservation. She liked to mountain bike. She told me about how she used to hit the trails her father when she was a teenager every weekend. He had died from lung cancer. She had gotten used to biking alone. An antifreeze cocktail flowed in as her blood flowed out. I always asked new members why they chose to be preserved. She told me more about her father. He'd arrived in this country from the former Second World. He had read about the far future and computers and robots in Asimov and Heinlein as a child in translation. When his polytechnic bought an old Russian computer, he applied to use it, and kept the first card he punched for it in his wallet until he died. He moved to his new home and worked on a computer every day. She said that he came home each day with a smile on his face. It was the look of a man who was living in a future that had once seemed centuries away. She wanted to travel through time too. I adjusted the packs of ice next to her head. The nurse began removing her jewelry. She removed a necklace from the patient, and flipped open the pendant. It was a photo of father and daughter at Cape Canaveral. Engraved on the back were a few lines in a language I could not read. I imagine that it is a promise they have made to each other. The nurse places it in a bag that will go to the mother. I hope the patient gets it back. With the nurse's help, I placed her on a gurney and move her to the van. Her core temperature was then just above freezing. She is pale. I noticed a tattoo that had been hidden beneath her watch. It is of a spiral galaxy, as though its rotation was how she truly wanted to measure time. She was placed in a precooling chamber. She was slowly brought down to temperature before being placed in one of the larger tanks. She will be upside down so that if there is a systems failure, the head will thaw last when the liquid nitrogen boils away. Is she already with her father? As a spirit or soul? Has she joined him in the universe's entropy? She might soon have a million stories she would want to share with him. I said a quiet goodbye and closed my eyes as I shut the chamber. I open my eyes. She is standing over me. She is eight. She kisses me on the forehead and I pull her towards me. I rub the sleep from my eyes. I feel sharp pains emanating from within my chest. I cough for a moment, and then pull her back towards me. "What will we do today, Daddy? " , she asks, smile gleaming. I stifle another cough. "Plan for the future."

According to the World Health Organization, breast cancer is the most common form of cancer in women. It is the second leading cause of death among women round the world, becoming the most fatal form of cancer. Despite the existence of several imaging techniques useful to aid at the diagnosis of breast cancer, x-ray mammography is still the most used and effective imaging technology. Consequently, mammographic image segmentation is a fundamental task to support image analysis and diagnosis, taking into account shape analysis of mammary lesions and their borders. However, mammogram segmentation is a very hard process, once it is highly dependent on the types of mammary tissues. The GrowCut algorithm is a relatively new method to perform general image segmentation based on the selection of just a few points inside and outside the region of interest, reaching good results at difficult segmentation cases when these points are correctly selected. In this work we present a new semi-supervised segmentation algorithm based on the modification of the GrowCut algorithm to perform automatic mammographic image segmentation once a region of interest is selected by a specialist. In our proposal, we used fuzzy Gaussian membership functions to modify the evolution rule of the original GrowCut algorithm, in order to estimate the uncertainty of a pixel being object or background. The main impact of the proposed method is the significant reduction of expert effort in the initialization of seed points of GrowCut to perform accurate segmentation, once it removes the need of selection of background seeds. Furthermore, the proposed method is robust to wrong seed positioning and can be extended to other seed based techniques. These characteristics have impact on expert and intelligent systems, once it helps to develop a segmentation method with lower required specialist knowledge, being robust and as efficient as state of the art techniques. We also constructed an automatic point selection process based on the simulated annealing optimization method, avoiding the need of human intervention. The proposed approach was qualitatively compared with other state-of-the-art segmentation techniques, considering the shape of segmented regions. In order to validate our proposal, we built an image classifier using a classical multilayer perceptron. We used Zernike moments to extract segmented image features. This analysis employed 685 mammograms from IRMA breast cancer database, using fat and fibroid tissues. Results show that the proposed technique could achieve a classification rate of 91.28 for fat tissues, evidencing the feasibility of our approach.

"Our sensor uses only biological materials such as proteins, sugars and lipids because it was developed from natural sources like insects and plants" says Dr. Shinya Imai who led the research group. Marx extensively discussed societal issues and structures, relating them to governance and economics, but did not offer concrete solutions. Much has been written about what socialism and communism entail, yet there is limited discussion on how these systems function. Therefore, I argue that communism fails on paper due to the majority of its principles being philosophical rather than practical. It is important to note that communism pertains to the economic structure, not the government. Various forms of communism attempt to address the "how," but none succeed on paper as they fail to meet the foundational tenets of what communism represents.

We show how to extend traditional intrinsic image decompositions to incorporate further layers above albedo and shading. It is hard to obtain data to learn a multi-layer decomposition. Instead, we can learn to decompose an image into layers that are "like this" by authoring generative models for each layer using proxy examples that capture the P latonic ideal (Mondrian images for albedo; rendered 3D primitives for shading; material swatches for shading detail). Our method then generates image layers, one from each model, that explain the image. Our approach rests on innovation in generative models for images. We introduce a Convolutional Variational Auto Encoder (conv-VAE), a novel VAE architecture that can reconstruct high fidelity images. The approach is general, and does not require that layers admit a physical interpretation.

Bacteria often attach to surfaces and form dense aggregations called biofilms or bacterial mats. These films can range from a few micrometers in thickness to up to half a meter in depth, and may contain multiple species of bacteria, protists and archaea. Bacteria living in biofilms display a complex arrangement of cells and extracellular components, forming secondary structures, such as microcolonies, through which there are networks of channels to enable better diffusion of nutrients. In natural environments, such as soil or the surfaces of plants, the majority of bacteria are bound to surfaces in biofilms. Biofilms are also important in medicine, as these structures are often present during chronic bacterial infections or in infections of implanted medical devices, and bacteria protected within biofilms are much harder to kill than individual isolated bacteria.

One of the most challenging problems in computational advertising is the prediction of click-through and conversion rates for bidding in online advertising auctions. An unaddressed problem in previous approaches is the existence of highly non-uniform misprediction costs. While for model evaluation these costs have been taken into account through recently proposed business-aware offline metrics - such as the Utility metric which measures the impact on advertiser profit - this is not the case when training the models themselves. In this paper, to bridge the gap, we formally analyze the relationship between optimizing the Utility metric and the log loss, which is considered as one of the state-of-the-art approaches in conversion modeling. Our analysis motivates the idea of weighting the log loss with the business value of the predicted outcome. We present and analyze a new cost weighting scheme and show that significant gains in offline and online performance can be achieved.

We consider convolutional networks from a reproducing kernel Hilbert space viewpoint. We establish harmonic decompositions of convolutional networks, that is expansions into sums of elementary functions of increasing order. The decompositions can be viewed as generalizations of the Fourier series for periodic functions or the Taylor series for smooth functions. In this case, the elementary functions are called "convolutional harmonics," which are a family of functions representing the different frequencies of the convolution operation. The use of convolutional harmonics allows us to better understand and interpret the behavior of convolutional networks, and also provides a framework for designing more efficient and effective network architectures. Additionally, the theory of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces provides a rigorous mathematical foundation for studying convolutional networks and their properties.

A significant challenge in addressing continuous Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) lies in inferring the multimodal distribution of the underlying true states and making the planning algorithm sensitive to perception errors. We frame POMDP filtering and planning tasks as two interconnected Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) processes—one operating over actual states and the other over future optimal paths—and integrate their advantages into a novel model called the DualSMC network. Specifically, we introduce an adversarial particle filter that utilizes the adversarial relationship among its internal components. Using the filtering outcomes, we develop a planning algorithm that enhances the existing SMC approach for continuous POMDPs by incorporating an uncertainty-aware policy. Importantly, DualSMC effectively handles complex observations, such as image inputs, and maintains high interpretability. It has been demonstrated to perform well in three continuous POMDP domains: floor positioning, 3D light-dark navigation, and a modified Reacher environment. The code is available at footnote 2.

Primary resistance occurs when a person becomes infected with a resistant strain of TB. A person with fully susceptible MTB may develop secondary (acquired) resistance during therapy because of inadequate treatment, not taking the prescribed regimen appropriately (lack of compliance), or using low-quality medication. Drug-resistant TB is a serious public health issue in many developing countries, as its treatment is longer and requires more expensive drugs. MDR-TB is defined as resistance to the two most effective first-line TB drugs: rifampicin and isoniazid. Extensively drug-resistant TB is also resistant to three or more of the six classes of second-line drugs. Totally drug-resistant TB is resistant to all currently used drugs. It was first observed in 2003 in Italy, but not widely reported until 2012, and has also been found in Iran and India. Bedaquiline is tentatively supported for use in multiple drug-resistant TB.

Scholars analyzing responses on social media often use either intricate behavioral models or specific platform indicators like retweets, hashtags, links, or mentions. Much of the content on social platforms is challenging to model due to the varied and incomplete understanding of human expression. We propose content transfer, an information-theoretic metric with predictive significance, which measures the impact of one user's content on another in a model-free manner. This measure can be calculated by integrating recent developments in non-parametric entropy estimation with advanced techniques for content representation. Our experiments on Twitter data show that content transfer effectively captures meaningful, predictive connections between users, even when they are not connected through followers or mentions. We argue that this approach enables the analysis of previously overlooked social media content using rigorous statistical methods.

An Analysis of Count William Reary's Argument Against Sir Tantey's Conclusions About Interdimensional Beings In his essay, An Argument Against Sir Tantey's Conclusions About Interdimensional Beings, famed author, columnist, and essayist Count William Reary argues that Tantey's conclusions lack supporting scientific evidence, writing that " unless one can simply will imaginary sentient lifeforms into existence, Sir Tantey's ideas have no basis whatsoever in science, logic, or even common sense. " Reary scatters effective rhetorical strategies throughout his paper, weaving clever analogies, metaphors, and even emotional appeals within it, providing more than sufficient support to his persuasive argument that Tantey's conclusions are, as he puts it, " bunk to anyone with half a brain and at least the primitive ability to use tools. " The most central aspect of Reary's means of persuasion are his rather surprising and exaggerated appeals to the emotion of his readers, making use of the pride they have in their identity as human beings, as well as members of the technologically advanced first world nations spangling the planet. He uniquely uses this emotion to support science-based thinking, as in the start of his second paragraph, where he writes that " we as a species have advanced far, far beyond other animal orgasms (sic) on the planet by making use of our incredible ability to identify what is true and what is not through a long-developed thinking called ' the scientific method ', and we should not allow ignorant halfwits like Tantey to taint our vast collection of knowledge with his cult-like beliefs in yellow-coloured, tentacle-infused aliens passing through invisible doors to mess with our banking systems. " Reary knows that the readers of his newspaper, The Weekly Reary, have pride in logic and despise extraordinary claims made without extraordinary evidence, and he uses these attributes to his advantage by using ad hominem attacks against Tantey, calling him an " ignorant halfwit. " Reary's less critical, less emotional support includes his analogies, such as one where he compares making conclusions about other realities to " believing that the bats in a cave are white, without even first confirming the existence of the cave. " His simple and easy-to-understand comparisons are very effective, especially considering the ironically low level of education his readers actually have. More complex analogies wouldn't achieve the effect Reary was going for - indeed, that is not what analogies are for. Analogies are supposed to be a simple, understandable comparison, and Reary knows exactly what he is doing. Reary also uses colorful and creative metaphors in order to captivate his readers, painting pictures in their minds with clever imagery and building in their brains an indestructible structure labeled " we are great. " His arguably most effective metaphor is when he says that " the human power of logic and science is a firm foundation upon which we build our cities, our efforts, and our pride. " He then compares this foundation to Tantey's " shakey, weak bridge upon which he transports the animalistic natives he calls his ' undeniable conclusions. These metaphors paint Reary and the rest of humanity as the inhabitants of incredible cities, and Tantey as the lone builder of an insufficient bridge used by tribal people. In conclusion, it is certain that Reary makes a compelling argument against Tantey's strange, almost schizophrenic ramblings. It is an argument that is most definitely effective at convincing his simple, easily-persuaded readers that Tantey does indeed make " shitty conclusions ," and that maybe he should be locked up in a " goddamn mental asylum " so he does not hurt other people.

Quantum annealing (QA) is a quantum computing algorithm that works on the principle of Adiabatic Quantum Computation (AQC), and it has shown significant computational advantages in solving combinatorial optimization problems , which are very common for applications such as problem-solving with biological compounds. However, current QA algorithms suffer from poor robustness to noise in their input signals. One way around this limitation would be through the use of novel noise sources: entangled pairs of photons or superpositions of photons can amplify QA's output signal by orders of magnitude without affecting its robustness. To date, experiments using entangled photons have yielded limited gains due to thermal noise arising during transmission between parties involved in these experiments. In addition, there exists no efficient way to interactively control the temperature at each end of the experiment so as to obtain more useful results over time.

We address the task of identifying densely connected subsets of multivariate Gaussian random variables within a graphical model framework. We propose two novel estimators based on the Ordered Weighted 1 (OWL) norm: 1) The Graphical OWL (GOWL) is a penalized likelihood method that applies the OWL norm to the lower triangle components of the precision matrix. 2) The column-by-column Graphical OWL (ccGOWL) estimates the precision matrix by performing OWL regularized linear regressions. Both methods can simultaneously identify highly correlated groups of variables and control the sparsity in the resulting precision matrix. We formulate GOWL such that it solves a composite optimization problem and establish that the estimator has a unique global solution. In addition, we prove sufficient grouping conditions for each column of the ccGOWL precision matrix estimate. We propose proximal descent algorithms to find the optimum for both estimators. For synthetic data where group structure is present, the ccGOWL estimator requires significantly reduced computation and achieves similar or greater accuracy than state-of-the-art estimators. Timing comparisons are presented and demonstrates the superior computational efficiency of the ccGOWL. We illustrate the grouping performance of the ccGOWL method on a cancer gene expression data set and an equities data set.

The majority of works in distributed storage networks assume a simple network model with a collection of identical storage nodes with the same communication cost between the nodes. In this paper, we consider a realistic multi-rack distributed data storage network and present a code design framework for this model. Considering the cheaper data transmission within the racks, our code construction method is able to locally repair the nodes failure within the same rack by using only the survived nodes in the same rack. However, in the case of severe failure patterns when the information content of the survived nodes is not sufficient to repair the failures, other racks will participate in the repair process. By employing the criteria of our multi-rack storage code, we establish a linear programming bound on the size of the code in order to maximize the code rate.

This paper considers a network of stochastic evidence accumulators, each represented by a drift-diffusion model accruing evidence towards a decision in continuous time by observing a noisy signal and by receiving a time-varying external input. In a mean-field scenario, the influence of one agent on the other is effectively captured by the mean field associated with the distribution of the decision variables. We present an approximate mean-field model to describe the population dynamics of the network. We derive approximate mean-field equations of the decision variables in terms of the distribution of the decision variables, and obtain a closed-form expression of the expected time to reach a decision in the asymptotic limit. Moreover, we show that when the decision problem can be linearly decomposed into subproblems, the mean-field model can be reduced to a set of independent subproblems. These results provide a rigorous mean-field approximation of the population dynamics of stochastic evidence accumulators in continuous time. We discuss extensions of the mean-field model and provide a numerical comparison of the mean-field model with the original system for a specific example.

Der inference von Straßengraphen aus Satellitenaufnahmen ist eine schwierige Aufgabe im Computer Vision. Bestehende Lösungen lassen sich in zwei Kategorien unterteilen: (1) Pixel-basierte Segmentierungsmethoden, die feststellen, ob ein bestimmter Pixel auf einer Straße liegt, und (2) Graph-basierte Ansätze, die den Straßengraphen schrittweise vorhersagen. Wir finden, dass diese beiden Ansätze Vorteile besitzen, jedoch auch ihre eigenen Grenzen haben. In dieser Arbeit vorschlagen wir eine neue Methode namens Sat2Graph, die die Vorzüge beider Kategorien in einem einheitlichen Framework kombiniert. Der Schlüsselgedanke von Sat2Graph besteht in einer neuen Kodierungsschemazu, dem Graph-Tensor-Kodierung (GTE), das den Straßengraphen in eine Tensor-Vertretung codiert. GTE ermöglicht es, einen einfachen, nicht rekursiven, supervised Model zu trainieren, um eine Vielzahl von Merkmalen direkt aus der Bildinformation abzuleiten, die die Struktur des Graphs beschreiben. Wir evaluieren Sat2Graph mit zwei großen Datensätzen. Wir zeigen, dass Sat2Graph besser als bisherige Methoden auf zwei weit verbreiteten Metriken, TOPO und APLS, performt. Zudem können zwar bisher nur planare Straßengraphen inferiert werden; unser Ansatz ist in der Lage, überpassende Straßen (wie Überbrücke) zu inferieren und dies robust durchzuführen.

Extracting appropriate features to represent a corpus is an important task for textual mining. Previous attention based work usually enhance feature at the lexical level, which lacks the exploration of feature augmentation at the sentence level. In this paper, we exploit a Dynamic Feature Generation Network (DFGN) to solve this problem. Specifically, DFGN generates features based on a variety of attention mechanisms and attaches features to sentence representation. Then a thresholder is designed to filter the mined features automatically. DFGN extracts the most significant characteristics from datasets to keep its practicability and robustness. Experimental results on multiple well-known answer selection datasets show that our proposed approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. We give a detailed analysis of the experiments to illustrate why DFGN provides excellent retrieval and interpretative ability.

The essence of free trade lies in comparative advantage. This concept refers to the fact that each nation typically excels in producing certain goods or services due to a blend of factors like natural resources, educational attainment, and capital availability. For instance, Cuba is renowned for its cigar production, Germany for automobiles, Taiwan for semiconductors, among others. Free trade enables nations to concentrate on their strengths and avoid wasteful spending on areas where they lack expertise, as they can acquire necessary goods from other countries via trade. In contrast, protectionism involves government policies that make imports costly, thereby stimulating domestic production, often in specific sectors. However, this approach leads to a situation where countries become "jack of all trades, master of none," as domestic firms lack competition and tend to become complacent. A notable case is Brazil’s strict import restrictions on foreign computers in the 1980s, which hindered the development of its own computer industry, exacerbating the technological gap rather than bridging it. Similarly, the U.S. automobile industry faced challenges in the 1970s due to limited competition, resulting in subpar quality and reliability. When Japanese companies like Honda and Toyota entered the market with better products, they captured significant market shares, leaving American automakers struggling to maintain competitiveness. These issues highlight the drawbacks of protectionism, particularly when it restricts access to advanced technologies and stifles innovation.
