In recent years I have become a big fan of Major League Baseball, watching dozens of games of my team (the Rockies) and following the playoffs. That said, the regular season is too long in terms of the number of games played. Every team plays 162 games per season plus 29 spring training games immediately prior to the season's opening. That's roughly double the amount of games in the NBA regular season, and roughly ten times the number of games in the NFL regular season. This means that every team will play 5-6 games per week, except during the relatively short all-star break, for close to seven months (excluding the postseason). This has a number of negative effects. First, it leads to position players being injured through the wear-and-tear of playing so often. How often is a starting position player put out of commission for a couple weeks because of a tweaked hamstring or shoulder soreness or knee pain? Starting position players often have to be rested even when teams are in still in the hunt for a playoff berth just to avoid these wear-and-tear injuries. Second, the sheer number of games hinders baseball's ability to be a more national sport like basketball or football. There are so many games that just trying to follow your local team will provide more than enough baseball for a year. I don't often feel motivated to watch a Yankees vs. Red Sox game on national TV when I have already seen 5 Rockies' games during the week. Compare with other major sports, especially football, where you can follow your team and still have plenty of time to follow the rest of the action. This is partially what allows football and basketball to be national sports and thus be more relevant in the national culture. The fatigue due to the number of games played dramatically reduces ratings for games on national TV. Third, the number of games also decreases local television ratings and fan attendance at the stadiums. When there are 162 games, there's no sense of missing out if you miss a game or five during the season, because no individual game is of much importance in itself (save for the last 20-30 games of the season played by a handful of the 30 teams chasing a playoff berth in September). This is especially true in the mid-season slog during June, July, and early August. Fourth, it makes it harder for casual fans to become more devoted fans because it is just hard to follow a team with so many games to be played. It requires a great deal of motivation and time investment to become a more devoted fan, especially if your team isn't contending. Fifth, and finally, the number of games means that the season must be very long in terms of time. Spring training starts at the beginning of March, while the World Series is played at the end of October. This causes two major problems. First, because baseball cannot be played in rough weather, and most teams play in open stadiums, this leads to a risk of games being cancelled due to snow in the early part of the season and the late part of the season and, crucially, during the playoffs. Second, this means that baseball must overlap with football at the end of the season which, given the utter dominance of football in the ratings and in sports coverage in the news, can only siphon fan attention and interest away from baseball right when it should be heating up. I believe the regular season should be shortened by at least 20 games, and perhaps as many as 50-60, to deal with the above five issues. So, Reddit, change my view! Hello, users of CMV! QoS-based Web service recommendation has recently gained much attention for providing a promising way to help users find high-quality services. To facilitate such recommendations, existing studies suggest the use of collaborative filtering techniques for personalized QoS prediction. These approaches, by leveraging partially observed QoS values from users, can achieve high accuracy of QoS predictions on the unobserved ones. However, the requirement to collect users' QoS data likely puts user privacy at risk, thus making them unwilling to contribute their usage data to a Web service recommender system. As a result, privacy becomes a critical challenge in developing practical Web service recommender systems. In this paper, we make the first attempt to cope with the privacy concerns for Web service recommendation. Specifically, we propose a simple yet effective privacy-preserving framework by applying data obfuscation techniques, and further develop two representative privacy-preserving QoS prediction approaches under this framework. Evaluation results from a publicly-available QoS dataset of real-world Web services demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of our privacy-preserving QoS prediction approaches. We believe our work can serve as a good starting point to inspire more research efforts on privacy-preserving Web service recommendation.

The probe is equipped with enough hardware and software to perform the maneuver independently. Therefore, ground control only needs to issue commands specifying where to direct the probe, when to ignite the engines, when to extinguish them, and how various instruments should behave under normal conditions or if there are issues. The probe typically has numerous sensors, such as a wide-angle camera to detect stars, a built-in star map to determine its rotational position, and the ability to observe the Sun or planets to estimate its location within the solar system. It may also attempt to align itself optimally to receive signals from Earth and adjust its orientation accordingly.

From Earth, we can retrieve telemetry data from the probe. We can measure the angle at which signals arrive and the time it takes for the probe to respond, enabling us to determine its location. We can also analyze the Doppler effect to calculate the probe's speed. By combining multiple measurements, we can achieve a relatively precise orbit for the probe.

When we need the probe to alter its course, we transmit a command specifying the direction to aim, the timing of engine ignition and cessation, and how instruments should react if everything proceeds smoothly or if certain instruments malfunction. The probe will then autonomously carry out these instructions and communicate back to Earth upon completion.

We present an approach to develop folds for nested data types using dependent types. We call such folds dependently typed folds , they have the following properties. (1) Dependently typed folds are defined by well-founded recursion and they can be defined in a total dependently typed language. (2) Dependently typed folds do not depend on maps, map functions and many terminating functions can be defined using dependently typed folds. (3) The induction principles for nested data types follow from the definitions of dependently typed folds and the programs defined by dependently typed folds can be formally verified. (4) Dependently typed folds exist for any nested data types and they can be specialized to the traditional higher-order folds . Using various of examples, we show how to program and reason about dependently typed folds. We also show how to obtain dependently typed folds in general and how to specialize them to the corresponding higher-order folds.

The growing use of mobile devices and imaging tools to capture and share documents has increased the demand for processing unstructured image data, such as retail receipts, insurance claims, and financial bills. Extracting information from these images poses significant challenges, particularly due to the presence of tables. Detecting and extracting data from tabular elements requires precise identification of table regions and their rows and columns. Although advances have been made in table detection, accurately recognizing the structure of tables remains difficult because it involves detailed analysis of row and column relationships. Previous methods addressed these issues separately using distinct models. In this study, we introduce TableNet, a new end-to-end deep learning framework designed to handle both table detection and structural recognition simultaneously. The model leverages the relationship between these two tasks to identify and extract table and column regions. Subsequently, semantic rules are applied to automatically extract rows from identified table areas. The developed model and method were tested on public datasets like ICDAR 2013 and Marmot Table, achieving state-of-the-art results. We also show that incorporating additional semantic features enhances model performance and demonstrates cross-dataset transferability. An added value of this work is providing enhanced table structure annotations for the Marmot dataset, which currently only includes table detection annotations.

Virtually every tech company relies on open-source projects where developers often work for free. Developers contribute to code to sharpen their skills, gain perspectives from the community, or just to help the industry. When open-source software is maintained on a voluntary basis, sometimes projects are abandoned or mistakes aren't corrected in a timely manner. Some open-source developers end up being hired by companies to maintain support for the code. However, as the code is free for anyone to use, companies may be reluctant to pay for the work, which will often benefit competitors. High-performance implementations of graph algorithms are challenging toimplement on new parallel hardware such as GPUs because of three challenges: (1) the difficulty of coming up with graph building blocks, (2) their vast dimensionality and (3) the need for large amounts of memory. Given that many graphs contain both directed and undirected edges between nodes, our goal is to design a runtime system in which we can use both memory and GPU resources in an intelligent manner. To support this goal, we designed and implemented a novel algorithm called DIMINI, which has been shown to scale well even if it uses only parts ofthe entire GPU's memory. We will present the precise definition of DIMINI and its architecture; how we achieved fast execution times using both low-level and high-level programming languages; and why, compared to other existing techniques, DIMINI achievesstate-of-the-art results while requiring relatively minimal storage space. Finally, we show that some simulations performed on thousands of real datasets have revealed interesting properties about the algorithm's performance at different levels of complexity.

We present a local routing algorithm which guarantees delivery in all connected graphs embedded on a known surface of genus g. The algorithm transports O (g log n) memory and is SLIPk-optimal in the sense of routing by shortest paths. It is also optimal in the number of hops on any genus g surface. The algorithm is based on a novel parameterization of the space of all possible routes through a connected graph embedded on a surface. This parameterization allows us to construct a constant number of such routes per edge, each of which is guaranteed to deliver messages in the given graph. We also show that this parameterization can be used to construct an efficient distributed data structure for efficient local routing in any graph embedded on a surface.

Chloroplasts' main role is to conduct photosynthesis, where the photosynthetic pigment chlorophyll captures the energy from sunlight and converts it and stores it in the energy-storage molecules ATP and NADPH . When a plant or animal needs food, these stored chemical messages can be released into the body for use as fuel. Presumably, this process of harvesting light through photosynthesis has powered all life on Earth since its formation 4 billion years ago. However, there are exceptions: algae don't have chloroplasts but rather rely upon photoassimilation - they take up carbon dioxide directly instead using an enzyme called RuBisCO that uses electrons captured during normal respiration to draw down CO2. This means that even though plants do not need them, some freshwater species such as cyanobacteria (commonly known as blue green algae) still possess two sets of organelles because their ancestors relied solely on photosynthesis before switching over to ion transport. Blue green algae consume nutrients like glucose which would otherwise be too large for other organisms with more efficient mechanisms - something we humans benefit greatly from today when eating spirulina!

We examine a linear Volterra integral equation of the second kind featuring a sum kernel $ K(t,t) = \sum_{i} K_i(t,t) $ and derive the solution by expressing it as a combination of solutions to individual equations with kernels $ K_i $. Under the condition that these separate equations have solutions, this leads to a new series expansion for the overall solution with enhanced convergence characteristics. Examples are provided, including the first known Volterra equation addressed using Heun's confluent functions, which resolves a longstanding issue regarding the representation of such functions. The method proposed is applicable in physics through the use of Volterra equations with degenerate kernels.

We came to Bratalian for Restaurant Week 2014 and were very excited, given the excellent reviews. Although some aspects of our experience were good, overall it was weak enough that I don't think we'll be back. Service: We called at about 5:15 to make a reservation, but the line did that fax machine screechy sound. Okay, then! We'll take our chances! On the ride there (it's about 25 minutes away from us), we worried that the place would be packed because of Restaurant Week so we called. The hostess was very accommodating and cordial, promising us a table. When we arrived, however, our luck with service changed. We didn't have a single server. Our order was briskly taken by one waiter, the food was dropped by another, and our dessert order was taken and delivered by the manager. The place was pretty busy, but other tables seemed to have good service. We felt overlooked and kind of like nuisances! The biggest issue is that they added an 18 gratuity and then taxed it. This is not typical procedure for Restaurant Week and I resented not necessarily having the gratuity added (I guess), but being taxed on it - I think - is in bad form. Food: From the Restaurant Week menu, we had the meatballs and fried calimari and zuchinni to start. Then, for our entrees, we had the linguine clams and the salmon with a lemon-butter sauce. For dessert, we had the profiteroles and the ricotta cheesecake. I thought the food was fine. The fried calamari didn't have much seasoning and was overly greasy; the dipping sauce on the side was a simple, plain marinara. If the calimari is going to be so plain, at least offer something a bit zestier for dipping. The meatballs were below average. They are VERY large, but, again, there wasn't much flavor. They were also a bit dense and dry; we were hoping for plump, juicy meatballs. The entrees were much better. The clams in the linguine were big and so flavorful. My salmon was probably the best part. The skin was crispy, the fish was cooked perfectly, the lemon-butter was succulent, and the sauteed spinach was a lovely compliment. If I come back, I would get the same entree. I was really looking forward to dessert because of other reviews, but I gotta say, the ricotta cheesecake didn't live up to the hype. I thought it was too dense and bread-y. The flavor was fine, but I didn't finish it because of the density. It was like a having a mouthful of wet sand! The profiteroles that my boyfriend ordered were good. The pastry was flaky and what can go wrong with vanilla ice cream and chocolate sauce?We had a half carafe of red wine along with our food, which gave us about 3 glasses total. Atmosphere: It's a small restaurant, but it's very cute. It's decorated perfectly and arranged so that it's size is not a problem. It's lively - lots of groups. There were a few slip-ups that night: a tray of dishes crashed, the smoke alarm went off in the kitchen. No major issues, really. Just added to the fun. The biggest atmosphere problem for me is the broken lock on the women's room door. I struggled to get out of that bathroom for like five minutes, which doesn't seem like a long time until that's the amount of minutes you spend involuntarily in a bathroom. I had almost resigned myself to my new life as a bathroom-dweller, about to start fashioning a bed out of toilet paper, when I finally escaped. Bratalian, you've got to fix the door. Overall, it was just okay. The service was unexceptional and simply got the job done. The food was fine. Unfortunately, that's not really enough to have me come back.

In his book, Humanism (1997), Tony Davies calls these critics "humanist anti-humanists." Critics of antihumanism, most notably Jurgen Habermas, counter that while antihumanists may highlight humanism's failure to fulfil its emancipatory ideal, they do not offer an alternative emancipatory project of their own. Others, like the German philosopher Heidegger considered themselves humanists on the model of the ancient Greeks, but thought humanism applied only to the German "race" and specifically to the Nazis and thus, in Davies' words, were anti-humanist humanists. Such a reading of Heidegger's thought is itself deeply controversial; Heidegger includes his own views and critique of Humanism in Letter On Humanism. Davies acknowledges that after the horrific experiences of the wars of the 20th century "it should no longer be possible to formulate phrases like 'the destiny of man' or the 'triumph of human reason' without an instant consciousness of the folly and brutality they drag behind them." For "it is almost impossible to think of a crime that has not been committed in the name of human reason." Yet, he continues, "it would be unwise to simply abandon the ground occupied by the historical humanisms. For one thing humanism remains on many occasions the only available alternative to bigotry and persecution. The freedom to speak and write, to organise and campaign in defence of individual or collective interests, to protest and disobey: all these can only be articulated in humanist terms."

Eve had been living in the Garden of Eden for as long as she could remember. She felt safe and content in its lush greenery, surrounded by all the creatures that called it home. But one day, a strange and mysterious serpent appeared in the Garden and offered her something that would change her life: a bite of the Forbidden Fruit. The serpent told her it would give her knowledge beyond her wildest dreams, but warned her of the consequences if she ate it. Eve knew that she could be punished for disobeying God's commandment not to eat the fruit, but she was also drawn to the promise of knowledge. After much deliberation, Eve decided not to eat the Forbidden Fruit. It wasn't because she was ignorant of the consequence; she was well aware of the potential punishment. Instead, it was because of the knowledge that she already possessed. She knew that even though the Fruit may have made her more powerful, it couldn't make her happier than she already was in the Garden. K-Medoids (KM) is a standard clustering method, used extensively on semi-metric data. Error analyses of KM have traditionally used an in-sample notion of error, which can be far from the out-of-sample errors that are relevant to real applications. We propose here two forms of out-of-sample analysis: one based only on comparisons with other methods and another using hierarchical clusterings. Using simulated and experimental datasets we compare these various approaches both for their accuracy as well as for computational time and efficiency.

The Tattooed Baby, the Inkfant, the marked child, Cain.... I'd been given many names after my parents gave me my first. I never knew my mother for a moment; the doctors said it was the most difficult birth they'd ever seen. But my father had done what he could; he just wasn't cut out for the life I forced upon him by existing. I fast became able to brush aside the comments and the stares, but my father took them hard enough for us both. He tried in vain to shelter me from the cruelties of the world that didn't understand me, he tried his best. When I came home with my clothes burned and blood coming from my ear, it was his breaking point. My father left that night, and something terrible happened to the boys who'd bullied me, and then I never saw him again. That's when I began to refer to myself as Cain; and now I can't remember what it was before that. As if it wasn't enough to be born with medically inexplicable tattoos covering 60 of your body, the forces that be had to make things more exhausting for me. My marks were called tattoos because no one had another word for them, but they weren't ink and they weren't pictures. Furthermore, contrary to the thousands of tattooed folks who'd tried to make me part of some type of pilgrimage, my marks hold no meaning for me. Covering my face, my arms, my torso and legs is script I can not read; script no man can read. Scrawled on me from head to toe are words in a language either long gone or not yet written, and the only thing I know about them is that they tell the story of my life; the book of Cain. I know that's what they say. I know it the way you know the feeling of the wind or the face of a loved one; I was born knowing only one thing: The marks are your story. I was never told this by a person, never visited in a dream; I just know it as a constant, unchanging truth. I spent much of my youth attempting to decipher the code, I have notebooks piled upon themselves filled with transcriptions of the text, rearranged and mirrored and substituted and analyzed; but not one sheet yields a clue. My purpose, my path - they're as cloudy as the day I was born. The search for meaning consumed me, and without any support I allowed it to. I've spent the better part of a decade buried within the reams of paper I'd transcribed but they gave me no quarter and here I sit. This room is dark; a sliver of natural light cascades between the barnboards I hammered to the windows, dust floating carelessly on the imperceptible breeze from the radiator. A small flashlight on my desk casts it's beam onto my chest, and in the small mirror seated next to it, just for an instant, I could swear I read the words "Get off Reddit and go outside."

While all supernatural ideas share this characteristic, I do not believe one can claim a supernatural concept is more likely to be true than another. This principle extends to the possibility of a supernatural idea being true compared to its absence. In my perspective, there are countless supernatural phenomena that could be fabricated, and while some might be true, the probability of any single one being so is essentially zero. Even if many people believe a particular idea is true, this does not change the fact that it remains a negligible chance among an infinite number of possibilities. Compared to any other idea, it is merely a tiny fraction of an endless sea of falsehoods. The reason why any created supernatural idea is infinitely improbable lies in the fact that for every supernatural idea, numerous others can be imagined as contradictions. Asserting that one supernatural idea is more likely to be true than another or denying it is unreasonable; examples include the Christian God, the Islamic deity, fairies, unicorns, and 36 mechanical ducks governing the universe, among others. Solid State Drives (SSDs) are better than regular hard drives because they offer faster read and write speeds, increased durability, and lower power consumption. SSDs use flash memory to store data instead of spinning disks like hard drives, which makes them more reliable since there are no moving parts. The absence of these moving parts also means that SSDs can start up much faster than hard drives. SSDs are limited in the number of cycles because each cell in the storage can only be written to a certain amount of times before it fails. This is not necessarily bad, but it does mean that you should take extra care when choosing an SSD for your device. Data should be backed up regularly so that any issues caused by this limitation can be minimized.

In this paper, we focus on simplifying and compressing Transformer-based encoder-decoder models for end-to-end ASR tasks. By examining the effects of removing certain components, we introduce a more compact Speech-Transformer. Additionally, we assess the impact of lowering the numerical precision of our network's weights and activations while ensuring that the full-precision model's performance is maintained. Human face analysis is an important task in computer vision. According to cognitive-psychological studies, facial dynamics could provide crucial cues for face analysis. The motion of a facial local region in facial expression is related to the motion of other facial local regions. In this paper, a novel deep learning approach, named facial dynamics interpreter network, has been proposed to interpret the important relations between local dynamics for estimating facial traits from expression sequence. The facial dynamics interpreter network is designed to be able to encode a relational importance, which is used for interpreting the relation between facial local dynamics and estimating facial traits. By comparative experiments, the effectiveness of the proposed method has been verified. The important relations between facial local dynamics are investigated by the proposed facial dynamics interpreter network in gender classification and age estimation. Moreover, experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in gender classification and age estimation.

Our bodies consist of billions of small units known as cells. Like all living organisms, these cells age and eventually die, requiring constant production of new cells. Each type of cell performs distinct functions, and when a cell generates more cells, those new ones should carry out the same role as the original. However, occasionally, an issue arises where the new cells prioritize producing even more cells rather than fulfilling their intended purpose. As a result, these cells may generate additional cells that do not contribute to essential tasks. Creating new cells demands energy, leading the body to allocate more resources to the cells responsible for reproduction rather than those performing vital functions. Consequently, many cells fail to perform their duties effectively, while others struggle to produce high-quality cells. Factors that contribute to cancer include conditions that increase the likelihood of faulty cell replication and reduce the body's ability to eliminate harmful cells, preventing them from proliferating further. Similar to humans, other species also experience cancer, including cats, dogs, horses, fish, birds, and hamsters. The prevalence of cancer in humans is likely influenced by two main factors: humans live longer than most other animals, resulting in more frequent cell division and a higher risk of errors, and humans are exposed to various environmental hazards such as radiation, unhealthy diets, smoking, medications, and dishwashing liquids. Cancer has existed for as long as human civilization has endured.

How it works: -Both have the same ultimate chemical response in the body (increased dopamine and norepinephrine activity) but go about it in a slightly different way. -Ritalin (methylphenidate): blocks the reuptake of dopamine and norepinephrine by your neurons, so these two chemicals hang out and are active for a little bit longer than normal. -Adderall (mixed amphetamines): both increase release of dopamine and norepinephrine as well as blocks reuptake. Same end result, chemicals hang out for a bit longer. -Both have a handful of other receptors that they bind to and have somewhat limited activity, but the above is the major mechanism of action. How your body breaks it down: -Both have peak blood concentrations at right about 3 hours after taking the dose -Ritalin has a half life of about 2-3 hours -Adderall has a half life of about 7-8 hours This results in Adderall more commonly being taken once a day vs twice a day for Ritalin. As to why one medication might work for one patient who tried and failed the other? Patient response does very, similar to how some patients respond to Zoloft but not Prozac (anti-depressants), both work on the exact same receptors in the body, but doesn't always result in the patient getting the same response.

We examine the process of transforming any weak online learner into a robust online learner. By introducing a fresh and intuitive criterion for weak online learnability, we design two online boosting methods. The initial method is an adaptation of boost-by-majority, which is proven to be nearly optimal in terms of the number of weak learners and the data requirements to attain a specific accuracy. However, this optimal approach is non-adaptive. Through the use of techniques from online loss reduction, we construct an adaptive boosting algorithm that remains parameter-free yet suboptimal. Both approaches utilize base learners capable of handling instance importance weights directly or employing rejection sampling with probabilities determined by the booster. Experimental validation supports these findings.

Synthesizing physiologically-accurate human movement in a variety of conditions can help practitioners plan surgeries, design experiments, or prototype assistive devices in simulated environments, reducing time and costs and improving treatment outcomes. The field is developing new techniques for motion capture that are faster than traditional video recording but still retain high quality (thousands to millions of variables) as well as the ability to simulate complex motions with ease." The findings were published November 1st in Science Advances by researchers from Washington University School of Medicine and Argonne National Laboratory. How does it work? A team at Argonne first trained an artificial neural network using images taken before and after people perform a series of exercises such as walking on leg extensions followed by knee extensions. Then they used this information to identify how different muscles contract during those movements - identifying their differences based off muscle activity patterns found in real humans' physical activities. They then fused these data points into computer models to create "graphics" depicting what muscles could move each way given specific instructions provided through software applications called "simulators." This allowed them to train synthetic models to imitate human biological actions like limb extension, bending forward, flexing hips back, raising arms overhead all while maintaining physical realism. In addition to reproducing realistic movements without needing special equipment, the method also helps scientists develop more accurate simulations because they know exactly where every individual parametric point has been located throughout the simulation process. In other words, if someone were to try out the potential application program again under similar circumstances, there would be less uncertainty about whether an action will occur and so results may actually get better. It's essentially another step towards creating prosthetics that feel and function just like natural limbs.

President Franklin D. Roosevelt advocated for a "good neighbor" approach aimed at improving ties with Mexico. In 1935, a federal court determined that three Mexican immigrants could not be granted citizenship due to their non-white status, which violated federal laws. Mexico objected, and Roosevelt opted to bypass this ruling, ensuring that the U.S. government considered Hispanics as white. Government agencies such as the State Department, Census Bureau, and Labor Department consistently classified individuals of Mexican heritage as white. This policy supported the League of United Latin American Citizens in their efforts to reduce discrimination by claiming whiteness.

The moment my roommates left for vacation, our house took on a different, darker persona. Something felt..... off. I believed at first that I was imagining things, but it quickly became apparent that this was not the case. I couldn't sleep for the footsteps outside my door. I couldn't turn off the lights for the breathing down my neck. I couldn't hide for the feeling of being endlessly watched. Something was coming, and I was nervous with excitement. I had been ready for this day for so long. My alarm goes off promptly at 6:04 AM. This is just enough time for me to leave my home by 7:19 and arrive at work at exactly 7:30, assuming normal traffic. The Wednesday after my roommates left I awoke as normal. I walked in a tired, unsteady, painful daze to the bathroom and flipped the light switch. From the corner of my tired, sleep-filled eyes, I could see what appeared to be the dark silhouette of a person in the reflection, peering into the bathroom from just outside the window. Without thinking I immediately shut my eyes, let out a horrible screech to cover any sudden sounds, and opened the middle right drawer on the cabinet below the mirror. I had rehearsed this drill enough to know that the hammer was in the back of the drawer laying horizontally. I shattered the mirror, closed the bathroom door, and opened my eyes. "Thank God!" I sighed. "That was close. I nearly saw him!" I performed my morning routine normally and left for work without further incident. Upon returning home that evening, I was filled with a sense of dread. It was already dark on this cold Winter evening and everything, though normal, appeared out of place inside my home. The warm light of my incandescent bulbs (fluorescent bulbs are too hospital-esque for my comfort) seemed awfully cool tonight. Realizing that this deafening silence could at any moment give way to the sudden sound of a frightening orchestral piece, I quickly produced the phone from my pocket and commanded my house-wide speaker system to play Mika's "Grace Kelly" on repeat at full volume. "That should cover up any unexpected violin slides and screeches," I said with a smirk. I turned for no reason in particular toward the black television screen which faces opposite to the front windows of my abode. Though the matte-black screen of this relatively old plasma television blurred any reflections cast upon it, I could see a faint outline and the subtle facial features of somebody peering into my home from the darkened front yard. "Egad!" Without thinking I immediately grabbed the television remote from the coffee table in front of me and hurled it toward the TV screen with a quick cast of the arm. Immediately after removing the reflection I synchronously stomped my feet and clapped my hands twice, producing a sound just loud enough for my decades-old hand-me-down clapper system to recognize over Grace Kelly, triggering the descent of every set of blinds in the house. "You may break in and murder me tonight," I said coyly, "but you won't startle me first!" My sleep was interrupted early in the morning hours by a cold sweat. Whenever this occurs, I flail my limbs and body blindly and wildly before opening my eyes, lest I open them to see someone hovering just above me. Feeling assured that nobody is within my personal space, I slowly opened my eyes, just in time to witness a shadow slip out of my cracked bedroom door and down the hallway. I followed in hot pursuit, making sure to swing both my arms in full circles like the blades of a windmill to knock out anybody who may be near me but not visible. My assailant screamed in fear from somewhere ahead of me. I had him. The stomping of my feet caused the blinds to rise and fall over and over. The phone, always in my pocket just in case, signaled the resumption of my Grace Kelly-only playlist at maximum volume. The situation had suddenly turned spooky. I was losing control. In my efforts to tame the unsettling circumstances I had found myself in, I had only succeeded in scaring myself. Fright filled the whole of my soul and I collapsed. I activated my only remaining defense system. I tightly shut my eyes and flailed as crazily and violently as I could. My arms and legs became maces of war, deadly to anybody within a 3 foot radius of me. Suddenly the music stopped. I sat myself up to a motionless and silent position as the shadow from before - no, two shadows - slid closer to me, inch by terrifying inch. The lights turned on and before me stood none other than my roommates! "Jesus! When did you get back?" I shouted at the top of my exhausted lungs. Both of my shoulders and hips were dislocated. "Daddy, you're scaring me!" said the smaller of my two female roommates. She clutched the leg of the other, who stared angrily and with fiery eyes into my own. I was beckoned to follow. We walked into the kitchen, where the older roommate, Alice, spread her arms out in a grand gesture toward a kitchen counter littered with empty whiskey bottles. "What the fuck, David," she screamed. "What the hell have you done!? The TV is ruined and the bathroom mirror is shattered! Why wouldn't you let us in?" "When did you get back from London?" I stammered, dumbfounded. "London? We went to my mothers for one night and you wouldn't let us back in! How many time are you going to do this to us? We had to go all the way back to mother's and call a locksmith to let us in! And you know what I figured out? She's right. She's always been right. You're a pathetic shell of a man and I regret the day I recited those vows. You either need to get help for the drinking problem that - guess what - you can't even hide anymore, or you need to get out of our life." The child clung to her mother as if for life and shook with nervousness. At that moment I saw myself in her, and not just in her ears which everybody says look identical to mine, but in her soul. She was spooked. How long have I been spooked, I wondered? How long have I been living in a personal prison of spookiness and easy spookification? I stood up and looked down. "I've pissed myself," I slurred drunkenly as I swayed side to side with a breeze that didn't exist. "I've pissed myself and I need to..." I vomited and passed out. When I woke, I was alone. "Oh my..... It was just a dream..." I whispered to nobody. There was a note next to me, folded gently. "David, We need to talk. Sara is at mother's. We'll be back later. -Alice" I stood and walked into the kitchen. I opened a mostly empty bottle of bourbon and quickly downed what was left of it. "Just a dram..." I chuckled. My roommates had just left on vacation, and immediately the house took on a different, darker persona.

Using machine learning to analyze chest X-rays is difficult because the clinical labels required to train these algorithms are obtained through rule-based natural language processing or human annotation, both of machine learning techniques. In this study, we describe how to use machine learning to analyze chest X-rays. We show that a novel feature extraction technique, called "deep learning" was used to detect a pattern in the image. The technique involves extracting a set of features from an image and then using a mathematical algorithm to find the hidden patterns in the image. This technique is compared to the conventional methods of analyzing clinical text, and to a human annotation system.

Counter-argument: While it may be true that certain personal habits or lifestyle choices may impact one's appearance, it is unfair and inaccurate to claim that being unattractive is solely the individual's fault. Many factors beyond personal control can contribute to one's appearance, including genetics, health conditions, and socio-economic factors. Additionally, societal standards of beauty and attractiveness are largely subjective and can vary across cultures and time periods. Therefore, it is important to recognize and appreciate the diversity of physical appearances, rather than placing blame or shaming individuals for their appearance.

" Our cause is righteous and just, we will not falter. " The words did not seem so reassuring as the dropship shuddered its way free of the atmosphere. Galen looked around at the bleeding and broken men with whom he shared the passenger bay. There were about half as many of them as there had been the day before. He wondered if the other ships had suffered the same fate, or worse. It had taken the Paladins almost an hour of fighting to secure these few dropships, which had been in for repairs and barely flew. They also had to find people to fly them. There were a few civilian pilots in the group so that wasn't too hard. They may have gotten this far in their plans but that meant little as to their success overall. The assault on the repair base had taken a heavier toll on the Paladins than most were willing to admit. Morale was at a low and Galen wondered if he was the only one having doubts. Galen retreated into his thoughts if only to spare himself the sight of his wounded friends and the pain of those lost. He wondered if he himself would last much longer. Might there one day be a tombstone somewhere that read " Here Lies Galen McKray - Friend, Brother, Insane Cultist and Extremist. " Doubtful, he hadn't exactly made an official announcement that he was off to join the Paladins of Cleansing Flame. He was not so blind as to think they weren't crazy but no one else seemed concerned with all that was wrong in the small, corrupted, godless, near-lawless colony of Radom. The nickname " Sodom " was not without merit. Most of the decent people had already left to find a place where they could worry less about being robbed or killed (or worse) in the street in broad daylight. Knowing that made Galen feel less guilty about what they set out to do. The dropship slowed as it made its final approach to its destination. All of those months of planning had finally paid off. Some people were paid, some were " coerced, " some convinced, and some simply disappeared. All of this added up to a rash of hardware problems with the communications equipment on the repair base. As far as the ships in orbit and planetary defenses were concerned, the dropships had left the base for some training flights and to test the repairs. Oh, how they were wrong. They never suspected what might actually be going on inside those small craft, or how large their impact would be. They would soon find out. Everyone would hear the news. Every possible variable had been planned out. Hundreds of people were involved, even if they didn't know it. Arguably most important was the work of a graduate student from the Inner Colonies who wrote a thesis on the geological instability of Radom's moon. The Paladins now planned to make the most of this information, and hope the kid was as good a cartographer as he was a student. The Cleansing Flame the Paladins spoke so highly of would come in the form of a shower of shrapnel from the shattered moon burning up on reentry and destroying all below. All of the crime, corruption, and general vileness of Radom would be turned to ash, a monument showing the consequences of evil. A gleaming warning to others who would stray from their path. The surface of the moon suddenly went from being an uninhabited waste to a waste with a population of about 80. The plan went into motion. The dropships were not the only things that had gone missing from Radom lately. There was also an almost noticeable lack of mining equipment, spaceworthy food containers, O2 tanks, cutting and welding equipment, firearms, and computers capable of accessing the guidance systems of the planetary defenses. Galen wondered if someday someone would appreciate the irony of " making the villainous fall upon their own swords " as the more devout liked to describe it. One by one the teams called in that their " passengers " had arrived safely. Everyone piled back into the ships and sped off toward their next objective. Gaining control of a military ship with which to fan the flames in other systems was a secondary objective, but it was all they could do with their lives once the Spark was struck. In the next thousand years, there wouldn't be a single soul who didn't know who they were or what they had done. Most would not understand that it was necessary for the betterment of Humanity as a whole, much like how Galen doubted it now. Setting tens of millions of people aflame did not seem like a righteous act, even if they were evil, but he didn't make the rules. Concerns over the morality of the plan or doubts that it were possible were always met with the same response, " Our cause is righteous and just, we will not falter. " The plan for taking a ship was simple...if you were completely insane. Galen thought it relied a bit too much on the enemy's skepticism, but that wasn't his problem either. He was just there to shoot people who tried to resist their taking the ship. Galen had never shot anyone before, but some of the " reformed " who had joined the Paladins told him it was easy after you got over the nervousness the first time. He had mixed feelings about that advice. He tried to reassure himself that these people were just as bad as those on the surface and they would kill him just as easily as look at him. He was determined to shoot them first. They landed in the bay of the cruiser just as the orbital guns began to light up... Galen couldn't help but stare in awe, involuntarily mimicking the sound he imagined the guns making even though there was no sound in the vacuum. The streaks from the guns tore across the void and into the pale ball around the planet, setting in motion a set of events that could never be undone and would go down in history as either the best or worst thing they had ever done. The moon shattered into several large shards surrounded by dust. In a few hours, days maybe, that dust would circle the planet like water in a drain until finally crashing into the planet itself. The days of " Sodom Colony " would be done. The shock tactics must have worked because it took several minutes for the soldiers aboard the ship to notice that a large group of armed and uniformed individuals had been running through the ship tying people up, locking doors, and disarming people while their eyes remained glued to the displays showing live reports of the events. The city is a thing of endless smells. There's the smell of freshly made pretzels coming from the sales-carts on the streets, the smell of the perfume of the woman walking past you, the foul odor of a piece of dog shit it's owner didn't pick up. And then there is that smell you can't quite place your finger on, that smell that is all of the smells of the city sort of coalescing together into a smell that can only be described as the city. For years, I could smell it. Always. Almost every day. From birth to today. I could smell the leaves changing in fall and the new blooms of spring, the hot dogs during a summer baseball game and salted roads of winter. The only times I haven't smelled it have been when I was going to Disney World when I was 11 and when I could smell the beer and weed of my dorm. Other than that, though, it's been the smell of the city. Until today. Today, I can smell fields, and flowers, and miles upon miles of fresh grass, beautiful trees, blue skies, and clear water. I don't know why. I'm just a money man, after all. Not the outdoorsy type. But then I look into the restaurant and see her waiting there. Her name's Clara, some friend of my sister's. From Kansas or Montana or some place like that. And then I realize what I've been smelling. I've been smelling me and her.

The First Great Awakening was a revivalist and evangelistic movement that spread across Protestant Europe and British North America, particularly among the American colonies during the 1730s and 1740s. It left a lasting influence on American Protestantism. This movement emerged from compelling sermons that provided individuals with a profound sense of personal revelation regarding their need for salvation through Jesus Christ. It moved away from religious rituals, ceremonies, sacraments, and hierarchical structures, emphasizing a deeply personal connection to Christianity. By promoting spiritual conviction, redemption, and a renewed focus on individual moral responsibility, it encouraged introspection and the adoption of a new standard of ethical living.

After the disastrous defeat of the Prussian Army at the Battle of Jena-Auerstedt in 1806, Napoleon occupied Berlin and had the officials of the Prussian General Directory swear an oath of allegiance to him, while King Frederick William III and his consort Louise fled via Konigsberg and the Curonian Spit to Memel. The French troops immediately took up pursuit but were delayed in the Battle of Eylau on 9 February 1807 by an East Prussian contingent under General Anton Wilhelm von L'Estocq. Napoleon had to stay at the Finckenstein Palace, but in May, after a siege of 75 days, his troops led by Marshal Francois Joseph Lefebvre were able to capture the city Danzig, which had been tenaciously defended by General Count Friedrich Adolf von Kalkreuth. On 14 June, Napoleon ended the War of the Fourth Coalition with his victory at the Battle of Friedland. Frederick William and Queen Louise met with Napoleon for peace negotiations, and on 9 July the Prussian king signed the Treaty of Tilsit.

It is possible to use a mechanism based on a pistonless rotary engine such as the Wankel engine in place of the cylinders and valve gear of a conventional reciprocating engine. The vehicle using this type of power generating device (an electric generator) may be driven by an internal combustion engine or a motor, but generally, it can run only under the operation conditions provided for vehicles running with no engine at all. For example, when running down hill, the driving force required from the vehicle becomes large and therefore, if the output shaft of the generator were coupled directly to the drive wheel through a planetary transmission system including a sun gear, a ring gear, first and second drive gears and third and fourth drive wheels, the vehicle would need other devices like brakes etc., making the whole configuration complicated. In addition, the efficiency tends to decrease because of friction loss due to engagement between the engaging members and components during turning of the driving wheel.

We've been together for several years. She is my best friend as well as my lover, and we do almost everything together. I don't want to marry her because I don't like the marriage and divorce laws regarding assets and debts. I see minimal benefit to a legal marriage, but a big risk if we don't work out as life partners. She is happy with how things are, but I think she would like it a bit if we were "official." I'm a little older than her, I have a good paying professional job, own the house we live in, and have some money invested in stocks. I invest a large chunk of my pay. I know what is mine before marriage would stay mine, but I am planning to continue to pay off my mortgage and invest a lot of my income. She is still in school, working on becoming a high-paid professional too. She will likely take out more student loans in the years to come. I am pretty certain she will continue to spend a lot more money than me on things like lattes and clothes. I am totally fine with this, but if we shared finances I would feel like she was buying stuff I don't care about with "our" money, and the money I was saving would also become "ours." I don't want to get married and pretend our finances are separate, knowing that if we get divorced the courts will split everything 5050 (I live in a community property state, meaning assets and debts acquired during marriage are joint). I also don't want to do a pre-nup. To make it legit, both of us would need attorneys during the process, which is expensive. We already live like we are married, it seems silly to get the marriage certificate, and do more paper work to undo a big chunk of what the marriage certificate does. I'm also concerned that she would not like the pre-nup process, and it might make getting married not as fun. I am pretty certain I will accumulate wealth much faster than she. I want to share this wealth with her while we are together, but if for some reason we don't work out I want to keep what I have worked hard to earn, and not be responsible for any debts she may still have. Many times the lower earning person helps the higher earner to make more money. This is not the case with us, we split all the housework and stuff evenly. I'd be wealthier if I were single (mainly because I'd get roommates and charge them rent), but I have no complaints because I love living with my girl and spending some money so we can have a blast. On the flip side, I am pretty sure she will be wealthier with me than if single or with someone else. I know a lot about personal finance, I give her as much advice as she will tolerate (haha), and will encourage her to practice good financial habits and establish financial security of her own. We don't have kids, but if we do we will figure out a fair way to divide labor, because we are both intelligent and can work out a good deal for both of us. If we think it is best for her to take some time off to be a SAHM, I am confident we will figure out a fair deal, including some compensation for missed career building. Or, maybe she'll SAH the first few years, and I'll SAH the next few years. I think the reason we have these divorce laws is because most people don't plan ahead for things. Divorce law is a crappy one-size-fits-all way to handle the problem, better than nothing but it still sucks. I have no problem publicly committing my love to the woman I want to spend my life with, but will not go along with the government dictating how we handle our finances. I don't want to get married, ever. Edit: I have talked to her about all this. I also want to hear other opinions. Thanks! Edit 2: Her view on marriage changes a lot. Sometimes she thinks the whole thing is stupid and we should never get married, but sometimes she'll ask me if I want to. Mexican food has long been one of my favorites because it lends itself to great flavors, more than just spice, but great southwestern flavor, in my opinion La Ristra just missed the mark. I'm surprised by the other reviews on here, and maybe they were just having an off day, but I'm not sure I'll be back to find out. This can make the math of computing distances simpler for humans and computers. The process of generating poetry involves training systems to create text that mimics poetic expressions. Deep learning models can autonomously generate poetry by learning from a collection of poems and understanding their linguistic patterns. In this study, we introduce a method where we adapt GPT-2, a pre-trained language model, to the task of poetry creation. Our approach incorporates novel elements, such as generating poems that convey emotions and provoke similar responses in readers, as well as employing the language of dreams—known as dream poetry. Through this method, we achieve an accuracy of 87.5% and 85% in eliciting feelings of sadness and joy, respectively. The model is trained on texts related to dreams, enabling it to produce poetry that aligns with dream characteristics, scoring at least 3.2 on the Likert scale. All generated poems undergo crowdsourced evaluation, and we utilize the Coh-Metrix tool to assess the quality of the generated text.

The degree distribution is an important characteristic of complex networks. In many data analysis applications, the networks should be represented as fixed-length feature vectors and therefore the feature extraction from the degree distribution is a necessary step. Moreover, many applications need a similarity function for comparison of complex networks based on their degree distributions. Such a similarity measure has many applications including classification and clustering of network instances, evaluation of network sampling methods, anomaly detection, and study of epidemic dynamics. The existing methods are unable to effectively capture the similarity of degree distributions, particularly when the corresponding networks have different sizes. Based on our observations about the structure of the degree distributions in networks over time, we propose a feature extraction and a similarity function for the degree distributions in complex networks. We propose to calculate the feature values based on the mean and standard deviation of the node degrees in order to decrease the effect of the network size on the extracted features. The proposed method is evaluated using different artificial and real network datasets, and it outperforms the state of the art methods with respect to the accuracy of the distance function and the effectiveness of the extracted features.

It was the middle of the night, and I was sound asleep. The only noise in the house was the soft snores coming from my dog asleep on the end of my bed. Suddenly, my iPhone started to ring, and I bolted upright. I looked at the caller ID, and my heart skipped a beat when I saw the name: my grandmother, who had passed away just three days ago. I hesitated for a moment, not sure if I wanted to answer or if I even could answer. I took a deep breath and swiped to answer the call. My grandmother's face appeared on the screen, and for a moment, I forgot that she was gone. "Hello?" I said, trying to keep the fear out of my voice. "Hello, dear," my grandmother said, her voice soft and comforting as ever. "I'm sorry to bother you in the middle of the night, but I need to talk to you." I was frozen, unsure of what to do or say. Was this some kind of cruel joke, or was I really seeing and hearing my grandmother despite her passing? But as we continued to talk, my doubts faded, and the conversation flowed as naturally as it had when she was alive. We talked about everything from the weather to family news to our favorite memories together. It was like no time had passed at all, and I felt like I was talking to her in person. Eventually, my grandmother said she had to go, and I realized that the sun was starting to come up. I hung up the call, still in disbelief over what had just happened. The next morning, I called my mother and told her what had happened. She was skeptical at first, but when I told her the details of our conversation, she became teary-eyed and told me that she believed my grandmother's spirit had reached out to me. I knew that I may never be able to fully explain what had happened, but in that moment, I felt grateful to have had one more conversation with my beloved grandmother.

In 1881, Tesla moved to Budapest to work under Ferenc Puskas at a telegraph company, the Budapest Telephone Exchange. Upon arrival, Tesla realized that the company, then under construction, was using inefficient direct current (DC) dynamos. He proposed an alternating current (AC) system that would be more efficient and cost-effective, but was rejected by Puskas who favored the existing DC system. Tesla then resigned from the company, but continued to consult for them for a short time. In 1882, he moved to Paris, where he worked for two years as an electrical engineer at the Continental Edison Company. In 1884, Tesla moved to New York City, where he worked until his death in 1943. During this period, Tesla designed and built a number of revolutionary AC motors and generators, conducted experiments with new forms of energy production, and developed several patents related to radio and wireless communication. He also founded the Tesla Electric Light Manufacturing Company in 1886, which later became the Tesla Coil Company. His inventions revolutionized the way electricity was used and distributed around the world.

To be 80-5 and give away a 200-run lead is a problem in any Test, let alone one where you know the pitch is going to get more difficult to bat on later in the match. However, for as tricky as the surface became - and some deliveries did do a lot - there were too many dismissals in England's second innings in particular that were not down to the pitch. The tourists were shown the way initially by Ben Stokes and Jonny Bairstow in the first innings, then by opening pair Alastair Cook and Haseeb Hameed in the second. Yet, English collapses - Michael Vaughan has referred to a "little disease" when panic appears to set in - were common. Four wickets for 29 runs and then four wickets for 30 runs in the first innings, eight wickets for 68 runs on the final day. It ultimately comes down to a batsman's state of mind. When you get a difficult delivery or the ball misbehaves, it can be very hard to put that out of your thoughts, but that is what the very best are able to do. The ability to clear your mind and focus on the next delivery is a skill my Test Match Special colleague Geoffrey Boycott speaks of so often. Media playback is not supported on this device So it seems that the next three Tests in this series will be about England's mindset. Can they play every ball on its merits? Can they keep their chins up if they lose the toss? Can they be positive without being reckless? Can they remember that they have played some good cricket? Do they believe that they can beat India? The answers to those questions are not straightforward because India is such a difficult place to tour. We knew from the start that playing five matches here straight after two in Bangladesh was going to be difficult in terms of managing morale and keeping spirits high. England do not have to look too far into the past for inspiration. They came from behind to win here four years ago. Going further into the past, the 1984-85 tour led by David Gower that I was part of was a real success because the togetherness of the team helped us overcame everything that was thrown at us. Indira Gandhi, the prime minister, was assassinated hours after the touring party arrived. The UK's deputy high commissioner Percy Norris later suffered the same fate, a day after hosting a reception for the England team. England stayed out there despite fears the tour would be cancelled, then lost the first Test because of some questionable umpiring. Yet, England came back to win that series 2-1 and that is the mindset that the class of 2016 have to adopt. If they can, India can be beaten because we have already seen that these are two evenly matched sides. The hosts' only advantage is they have greater experience playing in these conditions. Off-spinner Ravichandran Ashwin, the world's leading Test wicket-taker this year, does not look too frightening when conditions are not in his favour. The same can be said for his partner in crime Ravindra Jadeja. These are bowlers that can be handled. India also have plenty of batsmen yet to register runs. Openers KL Rahul and Murali Vijay both need a score, as do Ajinkya Rahane and wicketkeeper Wriddhiman Saha. Yes, Cheteshwar Pujara is in good form and captain Virat Kohli was in stellar touch in Visakhapatnam - he scored 248 runs and the winning margin was 246, so imagine the boon it would be for England if they can remove him cheaply. Not that the tourists do not have personnel issues of their own. Ben Duckett, who has made only 18 runs in three innings, looks very unlikely to play in the third Test in Mohali. England got into a muddle by not opening the batting with Hameed in Bangladesh and now both Gary Ballance and Duckett have failed at number four. The next available option appears to be Jos Buttler, one of the most exciting limited-overs players in the world. Is he the answer in the top order of a Test line-up against the spinning ball? We just do not know. Add to that the fact Buttler has played only one first-class match in the past year and there will be a lot of pressure on him if he is chosen to play in the next Test. Anyone saying with certainty that Buttler is the cavalry to solve England's problems is making a very big statement. Spinner Zafar Ansari is another who looks set to miss out on playing in the third Test. He may well have been left out anyway in order for England to play a fourth pace bowler, but he had a poor time with both ball and bat in Visakhapatnam. Those two aside, the other players that England have used in this series will all feel good. Cook, Hameed, Joe Root, Moeen Ali, Stokes and Bairstow have all made runs. Adil Rashid is really looking the part as a Test spin bowler, James Anderson has made an excellent return from injury and Chris Woakes will be raring to go after being rested for the second Test. The only question England will have is over the fitness of Stuart Broad, who returned his best bowling figures in India with a strained tendon in his foot. India can be beaten and England certainly have the ability. Do they have the mentality? Jonathan Agnew was speaking to BBC Sport's Stephan Shemilt.

I peered out my front window: sure enough, they had erected their projector screen and begun to play the dying baby polar bear slide show I had seen at least a hundred times already. They could've at least made a new one: I had seen Perry and Popo and Patrick die so many times that it was beginning to lose its emotional impact. "Hey, missy!" A man in a suit had noticed me looking through my curtains and stormed up to my window. "You better lower the temperature this instant, or you'll be sorry when your heating breaks!" The radiator sales industry was on the opposite end of the annoyance spectrum; they tended to resort to scare tactics to try and sway my mood. Recently, they had threatened to impose a nationwide boycott on selling to me if I didn't lower the temperature in time for winter. In my mind, it was a dubious strategy: first of all, I didn't even need a radiator if I maintained the warmth outside, and second of all, their ham-fisted attempts to cow me made me angrier than afraid, thus keeping the temperature high. Their plans were miraculously not the worst of the bunch: North Face had threatened to somehow render all my clothing choices fashionably obsolete if I didn't comply with their demands for cooler temperatures. "Go blow hot air somewhere else," I shouted back at him. "Yeah, if you need someone to vent to, we're here for you." Another man approached him from across my front yard. Judging from his uniform, he was a member of the nationwide union of air conditioning repairmen. "Don't listen to these people, girl. Just keep trucking; we got your back." A woman with an ice cream cone hat joined. I was naturally predisposed to supporting the groups who strove to make me happy - the farmers, the convertible manufacturers, the beachwear industry - even though I knew most of them didn't give two shits about my actual feelings; they just wanted to profit off the warm weather. In the past, some assholes even had the bright idea of trying to make me angry in order to keep the temperature high, under the impression that it was easier than making me happy or something. Even after three years, I can still remember that annoying sun screen commercial that played 247 on the lawn of my third house. They hadn't stopped until I had gotten so angry that their equipment melted. "She's killing our jobs!" A spokesman from the hot cocoa industry threw himself onto the grass in what I can only assume was an attempt to elicit my sympathy. "The ice caps are melting day by day," the loudspeaker droned. Perhaps it was time to move again. It had only been a week, so most of my belongings were still packed in my boxes. At this point, was it worth bothering with even a semi-permanent residence? They would find me again, and they would set up their speakers and projectors and one-act-plays to try and sway my emotions. Settling down would never be a realistic option. As I slumped against the wall, a chill overtook me, and a cheer resounded from outside my window. "We did it!"

First of all your muscles can only pull and can't push. This is why we have opposing muscles (e.g. your bicep pulls [contracts] to pull your forearm in and your tricep pulls [contracts] to pull your forearm out). Your nerves conduct electricity. That is how your brain communicates with your muscles to tell them to contract or relax. To detect if your muscle is contracted or relaxed there is bundle of nerves called the muscle spindle located in the muscle. When the patellar ligament is struck it causes the thigh muscle spindle to stretch which causes electricity to travel through your nerves. This electricity is indicating that your muscle is stretched out (i.e. relaxed and not contracted). Obviously you can consciously bend and straighten your knee, but to be able to balance and walk there is also some subconscious behaviour that is occurring without you realizing it. When the thigh muscle spindle registers that the thigh muscle is relaxed it triggers an automatic tightening of it to ensure you don't fall over if you are standing. This is being artificially triggered by the reflex hammer.

Four of those on board, three soldiers and an airman, were stationed at RAF Odiham in Hampshire. The fifth, an Army reservist, was based in London. The Ministry of Defence said the crash near Kandahar air base appeared to have been a "tragic accident." It represents the third single biggest loss of life of British troops in Afghanistan since the conflict began. The families of all five servicemen have been told. Three of the soldiers on board the helicopter were from the Army Air Corps, based at RAF Odiham in Hampshire, the MoD said late on Saturday. A fourth member of the crew was serving with the Royal Air Force and was also based at Odiham, while the fifth man was an Army reservist from 3 Military Intelligence Battalion, in London. Maj Gen Richard Felton, Commander Joint Helicopter Command, said: "It is with great sadness that we must confirm that five UK service personnel have been killed in this incident which, at this early stage, would appear to have been a tragic accident. "Events like this, whilst mercifully rare, remind us of the risks our personnel face in their work in Afghanistan as we approach the conclusion of the combat mission later this year. "Our thoughts are with the families and loved ones of those who have lost their lives." Prime Minister David Cameron said his "heart goes out to the families and friends of those killed in this terrible tragedy." Labour leader Ed Miliband said it was "tragic and poignant reminder of the sacrifices made by our armed forces in serving our country with bravery and distinction." It is the first fatal accident involving a UK military helicopter in Afghanistan since the conflict began in 2001. BBC defence correspondent Caroline Wyatt said sources had suggested the cause of the crash may have been "technical problems" on board the helicopter, despite claims by the Taliban that its fighters had shot it down. She said the location of the crash - close to the border with Pakistan - has also led to speculation that the helicopter could have been taking part in a special forces mission. It is understood the helicopter was a Westland Lynx Mk 9. A Ministry of Defence spokesman said: "We can confirm that a UK helicopter crashed in southern Afghanistan today. "The incident is under investigation and it would be inappropriate to comment further until families have been notified." The crash is understood to have happened around 30 miles from the Pakistan border, near Kandahar air base in the Takhta Pul district. The deaths bring the number of British forces killed in the conflict in Afghanistan to 453. The fatal crash comes after a Nimrod surveillance aircraft exploded in mid-air while supporting Nato ground operations near Kandahar, killing all 14 servicemen on board, in September 2006. This incident remains the biggest single loss of UK life at one time in Afghanistan. In 2012, six British soldiers were killed when a Warrior armoured fighting vehicle in Kandahar province was hit by an explosion. The International Security Assistance Force (ISAF) coalition of international forces said it was still in the process of reviewing the circumstances of Saturday's helicopter crash. "Our thoughts and prayers go out to the family and friends affected by this tragic event," it said in a statement. Defence analyst Paul Beaver said all the indications are that the crash involved a Lynx helicopter, which he said has an "exceptional record." He said the light utility helicopter is likely to have been operating in "fairly mountainous areas," or in "challenging" terrain. "The key now will be looking at the weather," Mr Beaver told the BBC. "If enemy action is not suspected, which is what the MoD is saying, then you have to look at whether this might well be weather-related." The crash brings the total number of international troops killed in Afghanistan in April to seven. It comes after the last major helicopter crash took place in December last year, when seven Americans and four Afghans died. In August 2011, the Taliban shot down an American Chinook near Kabul, killing 30 Americans and eight Afghans in the deadliest single incident for US troops since the war began. Herbivorous animals can sometimes eliminate their prey species, though this is not common. Some herbivores, such as zooplankton, feed on unicellular phytoplankton and kill their prey through individualized interactions. Many herbivores consume only a small portion of the plant. Livestock may uproot grass at its roots, but most of it is merely eaten, enabling the plant to regenerate. Kelp is often browsed in subtidal kelp forests, yet it continually regrows at the base of each blade to counteract browsing pressure. Additionally, animals may be "grazed" upon; female mosquitoes alight on hosts temporarily to obtain proteins necessary for offspring development. Starfish can also be grazed on, as they possess the ability to regenerate lost limbs.

When the engine revs are too low, the car may stall. Additionally, there's an ideal range of revs that provides the greatest power output per fuel unit. Going beyond or below this range reduces the power available from the engine.  

You're essentially asking why gears exist. The answer is straightforward: wheels rotate slowly at low speeds and quickly at high speeds, but engines need to operate at nearly the same RPM across all speeds for optimal efficiency. This separation between the engine and wheels is achieved through gears.  

It's akin to a bicycle with gears. If you shift into the heaviest gear and attempt to accelerate, it requires significant power to move slightly. This is why maintaining a single gear is impractical.  

Driving in top gear continuously prevents the car from launching from a stop. Each gear has a specific speed range.
