OSNs often impose severe constraints on the query rate, hence limiting the sample size to a small number of samples per user (e.g., 106107). As such, traditional methods for characterising nodes based on graph statistics are not appropriate in this setting as they rely heavily on unbiased sampling across all users and their activity patterns bib27]; [bib26. In order to overcome these limitations we examine how unstructured data from an existing Twitter account can be used to infer information about its underlying network structure. Our approach relies entirely upon self-generated tweets; a property that makes our method applicable to unrestricted accounts where self-generated content dominates, like many corporations' corporate accounts or celebrities' personal accounts. We consider various properties at different levels of granularity ranging from topics, aggregated by hashtags, up to relationships between people within a set bounding box around a particular event location as observed over several weeks. By considering multiple types of edges, we show that simple frequency counts quickly become insufficiently specific when it comes to identifying individual actors with compelling behaviours. Instead we employ techniques borrowed from community detection literature to identify communities whose members exhibit similar characteristics. Using temporal ordering metrics, we further classify individuals into distinct groups called 'clusters', which share consistent behaviour across time. This analysis reveals much more than just cluster membership and allows us to quantify important aspects of actor's personalities (such as trustworthiness), communication styles (e.g., supportive vs. competitive) and behavioural propensities (e.g., healthy versus aggressive behaviour). Given the comprehensive nature of our results, we feel confident presenting them as valuable novel contributions to research in this area since the rich contextual knowledge gained provides insights beyond previously published studies relying solely on co-occurrence statistics. Furthermore our methodology may have broader applications outside social media, especially those involving other natural language processing tasks that benefit from using richer context. 1 Introduction {sec1} Recent years have seen rapid growth in popularity of mobile electronic devices and services. So far we have remained largely ignorant of the heterogeneity of usage patterns exhibited by end-users who interact with such technologies due to lack of adequate sampling strategies employed in previous investigations. While there has been substantial progress made towards understanding what motivates Internet users to use certain websites, e.g.[b20] among others, insight into why some platforms remain popular despite high churn rates remains lacking. The study presented here addresses this problem and examines whether the well established theory in marketing field holds true in digital domain: are human beings buying things because they were told to do so, or instead engaging in activities out of conviction? If consumers really want to buy products, shouldn't we see evidence of such desire reflected in the volume and type of interactions they make while consuming goods and services? Since customers tend to purchase items that provide immediate gratification rather than long term benefits, it follows that those purchasing habits will reflect short term emotional attachment to brands rather than tangible utility. To test this hypothesis, we build models based on the daily "likes," retweets and mentions generated by two prominent Facebook pages (Nike and Coca Cola posted them simultaneously): if we find strong correlations between emotions experienced by each page's followers and item purchases postulated above then this would suggest that these phenomena occur largely independent of one another. Moreover, in contrast to most previous work focusing solely on raw tweet frequencies we also account for timestamps associated with each interaction. They help disambiguate phrases including words referring to events Kaepernick is getting booed, places I'm looking forward to training camp!, objects The new Apple iPhone 6S etc. taken from Twitter feeds produced by millions of everyday users irrespective of any interest in technology whatsoever and serve therefore as key pieces of additional information that allow us to model real world phenomena occurring on a global scale. In addition we include basic demographic features of the target audience that helps predict each customer's state of mind during hisher actual experience with a brand. Having thus assembled an inventory of likes, shares and comments collected from both pages over the course of four months, we apply standard machine learning algorithms to learn latent factors describing observed trends in user engagement on the pages. Some research institutions demand researchers to distribute the incomes they earn from publishing papers to their researchers andor co-authors. In this study, we deal with the Impact Factor-based ranking journal published by Elsevier that is of high interest for those who have a subscription access to it on a regular basis. We first develop a model based on the ISSNs collected as part of our survey, which are used as an input into two competitive equilibrium models. The first one assumes authors only get paid for the articles that appear in Elsevier's journals (no income is distributed among co-authors). This leads to a relatively efficient allocation of resources under our cooperative setting. However, when authors also receive some fee in addition to article publication charges, the second model shows that more allocations are optimal than expected. First, due to differences between how much each author earns compared to all other co-authors and the editors, a large number of 'free riders' exist whose productivity does not increase if all others do not contribute. Second, since these free riders may be able to obtain better conditions at competing publications, incentives for them to publish their work in Elsevier are lower than expected.

NMT systems are vulnerable to minor alterations in input. The effectiveness of these systems is often assessed by evaluating translation quality under noisy inputs. This study introduces new metrics that quantify the degree of degradation and shifts in translation caused by small perturbations. The research focuses on models utilizing subword regularization to enhance robustness and conducts thorough experiments with the proposed robustness measures. Experimental results indicate that the introduced metrics demonstrate an enhanced resistance to perturbations when subword regularization techniques are applied.

In this paper we study decomposition methods based on separable approximations for minimizing the augmented Lagrangian. In particular, we study and compare the Diagonal Quadratic Approximation Method (DQAM) of Mulvey and Sanz-Serna with the Augmented Lagrangian Method (ALM) of Chambolle and Pock. We show that for the minimization of a convex function in a Hilbert space, the DQAM achieves an error comparable to the one of the ALM in terms of the duality gap and the distance to the exact solution, but the ALM requires a much higher number of iterations. This observation motivates the development of a new DQAM based on the symmetric rank-one approximation. This new method, which we call SQR1-DQAM, has a better performance than DQAM when minimizing a convex function. We also show that SQR1-DQAM performs similarly to the ALM for the minimization of the sum of a convex and a smooth function. Finally, we apply the SQR1-DQAM to the Landweber iteration for Tikhonov regularization.

In this paper, we propose a relaxation to the stochastic ruler method originally described by Yan and Mukai in 1992 for asymptotically determining the global optima of discrete simulation optimization problems. In the standard stochastic ruler method, a range of possible values for the global optimum is estimated by sampling from the objective function a large number of times, and this range is then partitioned into smaller intervals through a greedy search. The method proceeds by eliminating all but one interval in each iteration of the greedy search. However, if the true global optimum lies outside of the final interval, it is not guaranteed that it will be found; Yan and Mukai suggest a heuristic method to address this issue. In our proposed method, we maintain an accumulation of all the intervals returned by the greedy search; thus, at the conclusion of the procedure, we have a set of candidate intervals which are likely to contain the global optimum. We find that this method performs well; the average percentage of times that the proposed method finds the global optimum is 99.9 for a variety of test functions.

The Swiss cantons maintain a permanent constitutional status and exhibit a significant level of autonomy compared to other nations. According to the Federal Constitution, all 26 cantons are equally situated. Each canton possesses its own constitution, legislative body, executive branch, and judicial system. Nevertheless, there are notable variations among the cantons, especially concerning population size and geographic scope. The populations range from 15,000 inhabitants in Appenzell Innerrhoden to 1,253,500 in Zurich, while the areas span from 37 square kilometers (14 square miles) in Basel-Stadt to 7,105 square kilometers (2,743 square miles) in Graubünden. The cantons collectively consist of 2,485 municipalities. Additionally, there are two enclaves within Switzerland: Busingen is part of Germany, and Campione d'Italia is located in Italy.

Helper T cells produce T cell receptors (TCRs) that identify antigens presented by Class II MHC molecules. The MHC:antigen complex is further recognized by the CD4 co-receptor, which facilitates the recruitment of internal cellular components (such as Lck) necessary for T cell activation. Helper T cells exhibit a less pronounced interaction with the MHC:antigen complex compared to killer T cells, requiring approximately 200–300 receptors per cell to bind an MHC:antigen for activation. Killer T cells can be activated by a single MHC:antigen binding event. Helper T cell activation necessitates extended contact with antigen-presenting cells. When a resting helper T cell becomes activated, it releases cytokines that regulate the functions of various cell types. Cytokines from helper T cells boost the antimicrobial capabilities of macrophages and the efficacy of killer T cells. Additionally, helper T cell activation leads to increased expression of surface molecules like CD40 ligand (CD154), providing additional signals needed for B cell activation.

For a given positive integer $ k $, a $ k $-dominating set in a graph $ G $ is a subset of vertices where each vertex not in the set has at least $ k $ neighbors within the set. A total $ k $-dominating set, also called a $ k $-tuple total dominating set, requires that every vertex in the graph has at least $ k $ neighbors within the set. The problem of determining the minimum size of such sets in a graph is referred to as $ k $-domination and total $ k $-domination, respectively. These extensions of the classical domination and total domination problems are known to be NP-hard for certain graph classes, including chordal graphs, split graphs, and undirected path graphs (specifically for total $ k $-domination). However, recent research by Kang et al. (2017) demonstrates that these problems can be solved efficiently on interval graphs, with a runtime of $ O(V(G)^{6}k^{4}) $. We present improved algorithms for $ k $-domination and total $ k $-domination on proper interval graphs by reducing the problem to a single shortest path calculation in a derived directed acyclic graph with $ O(V(G)^{2}k) $ nodes and $ O(V(G)^{4}k) $ arcs. By avoiding the construction of all arcs, we achieve a runtime of $ O(V(G)^{3}k) $. These methods also extend to the weighted case.

We examine a data structure that extends rectangular multi-dimensional arrays. The dimensions of an n-dimensional array are usually represented by a tuple of n natural numbers. Each component of this tuple specifies the length of the respective axis. When viewed as an array, its shape is defined by a single natural number, n. A natural number can also be considered as an array with a shape defined by the natural number 1 (or any singleton set's element). This leads to a hierarchy of array types where the shape of an array at level l is a level-l array of natural numbers. This structure arises naturally when considering arrays as containers, enabling the definition of both rank- and level-polymorphic operations. The former is common in array languages, while the latter allows for partial selections across numerous hyperplanes, which is frequently practical. In this paper, we present an Agda implementation of arrays with levels. We demonstrate that the proposed framework enables standard rank-polymorphic array operations while providing type system assurances that indexing remains valid. We extend the concept of a ranked operator to apply to arrays of any level and illustrate why this could be beneficial in real-world applications.

Translation software already exists and is pretty good. (If only we could do the same with dogs, so I could have a conversation with a poodle.) But the technology needs to be refined, and more importantly, we need to make it seamless. My e-mail inbox is filled with updates about Google's translation technology, which I use quite a bit when I travel. But so far, I've always had to do it manually. I paste text into an online form, then click "translate." It's a tedious process, and I can't imagine how I would cope if I were traveling and needed to take a taxi. That's why I was so excited to see a post on Google's blog about its new voice recognition technology, which can translate the speech of one person into the language of another person. It works with the voice-recognition software in Google's translation app, which is available for Android and iOS. Here's how it works: You speak in your own language into your phone, and it translates your words into text. Then you can choose to speak the translated text aloud. If you do, the recipient of the text will hear your translated voice. You can even speak to a machine in your own language and have it translate your words into another language, which I found a little surreal. Of course, this technology is still imperfect, and we have a long way to go before we are as good at it as humans. In the translation I did for my own article, I had to correct the text it spit out. But I don't think it would be long before my voice translation app is as good as a human translator. And that's a big deal, because for the first time, we will be able to communicate with people who don't speak our language. How we can get there The big question is, how do we make this technology seamless? When we use a phone to make a call, we don't think about whether the person at the other end of the line speaks our language, and that's because the phone companies have already figured out how to translate the call into our language. Ideally, it would work the same way with translation software. I would just speak and the phone would translate into the other person's language. The Google blog post said that when the technology is perfect, you won't even need to switch languages to communicate with a person who doesn't speak your own language. I would love to be able to have a conversation with a person who doesn't speak my language. How to make that work For that to happen, the translation needs to be seamless. The phone app should take over and translate what I say. Google's blog post said that there's a possibility that the phone will be able to translate what I say into the other person's language while I'm still speaking. I can't wait to try that. Neural network binary classifiers are often evaluated on metrics like accuracy and F 1 -Score, which are based on confusion matrix values (True Positives, False Positives, False Negatives, and True Negatives). However, these classifiers are commonly trained with a different loss, e.g. log loss. While it is preferable to perform training on the same loss as the evaluation metric, this is difficult in the case of confusion matrix based metrics because set membership is a step function without a derivative useful for backpropagation. To address this challenge, we propose an approximation of the step function that adheres to the properties necessary for effective training of binary networks using confusion matrix based metrics. This approach allows for end-to-end training of binary deep neural classifiers via batch gradient descent. We demonstrate the flexibility of this approach in several applications with varying levels of class imbalance. We also demonstrate how the approximation allows balancing between precision and recall in the appropriate ratio for the task at hand.

Most studies on distributed storage networks focus on a simplified model consisting of multiple identical storage nodes with uniform communication costs between them. This paper examines a more realistic multi-rack distributed data storage setup and introduces a code design approach tailored to this model. By leveraging lower transmission costs within racks, our method enables local node recovery within the same rack using only surviving nodes from that rack. However, if the information available from these surviving nodes is insufficient to address failures, other racks become involved in the repair process. We use the principles of our multi-rack storage code to derive a linear programming bound on the code's size, aiming to optimize the code rate.

Katiya recalls the days when her people wore heavy fur coats and thick-soled boots, gathering food for the hungry. There was joy and celebration every moment, thanks to the hunters and traders. Katiya remembers. However, the world grew colder, taking away the warmth it once provided. Initially, the men returned with less food, their meals becoming just fat and bones. Furs and silks became rare, and Katiya only remembered the sweetness of sweets. "Why isn't there laughter, Papa?" she asked, observing his troubled expression. "Why are things changing?" He replied with a weary smile, promising it would get better, patting her head and she believed him. But it never did. Finally, hunters and traders returned empty-handed. The air filled with the cries of the starving. Sometimes, hunger brought illness. Katiya watched too many of her people vanish into nothingness. She feared she would be the last. Each morning, she woke with her father, watching him vanish into the dark alongside others, desperate. Each evening, she saw the sorrow and despair on their faces. Eventually, the world turned against them. No longer the hunters, they became the hunted. Wild beasts now prowled them with newfound strength, waiting for the right moment to strike, vengeful and powerful. Scene text recognition (STR) has been extensively studied in last few years. Many recently-proposed methods are specially designed to accommodate the arbitrary shape, layout and orientation of scene texts, but ignoring that various font (or writing) styles also pose severe challenges to STR. These methods, where font features and content features of characters are tangled, perform poorly in text recognition on scene images with texts in novel font styles. To address this problem, we explore font-independent features of scene texts via attentional generation of glyphs in a large number of font styles. Specifically, we introduce trainable font embeddings to shape the font styles of generated glyphs, with the image feature of scene text only representing its essential patterns. The generation process is directed by the spatial attention mechanism, which effectively copes with irregular texts and generates higher-quality glyphs than existing image-to-image translation methods. Experiments conducted on several STR benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of our method compared to the state of the art.

All the knowledge you possess is built upon a substantial foundation, much like bricks in a pyramid. You cannot skip directly from basic arithmetic to advanced mathematics; you must first master each intermediate step to understand the concept fully. It’s essential to learn these steps in the correct sequence to ensure your knowledge builds logically. While you might explain percentages as dividing a quantity by 100, this does not inherently translate into mathematical understanding. Visualizing concepts in everyday language does not necessarily align with the abstract symbols on paper. You need to develop this ability at some point in your learning journey. If you lack even these foundational elements, your brain will struggle to link what you’re teaching with the skills required. Without a solid base, constructing the pyramid becomes impossible. Effective teaching often involves starting from the end and identifying what the learner already knows or needs to improve upon, rather than forcing them to grasp a concept from scratch. Memory retention also poses challenges—if you lose pieces of the puzzle, you won’t be able to assemble the whole. It’s important to identify the most effective methods for learning, such as auditory, visual, tactile, or hands-on approaches, to enhance retention. Although I can guide you through dense texts on number theory, if you don’t internalize this material, it will be difficult to retain. Similarly, if you learn better through other means, you’ll likely succeed in retaining the concepts and eventually grasp more complex ideas.

Israel has a three-tier court system. At the lowest level are magistrate courts, situated in most cities across the country. Above them are district courts, serving as both appellate courts and courts of first instance; they are situated in five of Israel's six districts. The third and highest tier is the Supreme Court, located in Jerusalem; it serves a dual role as the highest court of appeals and the High Court of Justice. In the latter role, the Supreme Court rules as a court of first instance, allowing individuals, both citizens and non-citizens, to petition against the decisions of state authorities. Although Israel supports the goals of the International Criminal Court, it has not ratified the Rome Statute, citing concerns about the ability of the court to remain free from political impartiality.

I was born in the earlier years of the war, a beacon of life among fields full of death. But even something as innocent and joyful as a new person, a new life to be, new possibilities is tarnished when death surrounds you. I was soon to find that was my life, death. I enlisted at 16, well you were forced to at 18 under new legislation, but given the choice at 16 I didn't see reason to delay the inevitable for 2 more measly years. I knew of the war, it was drilled into us from young, at the ripe age of 10 we were taught who the enemy was, at 12 we were told of gruesome war stories, enough to wreak havoc on a young child's developing mind. Most of us born during the war knew more about death by 16 than life. From 16 through to 22 my life was the war, all I knew was the war, all I did was war. I had killed and seen others be killed, I had hid in bunkers cramped together with 20 other men, barely a centimemtre between us, waiting all night for the attrition to end only to rise alive from the thick concrete grave, and find the real grave was above us. The dead were above the ground, the alive were in the ground. That was the war, up was down, down was left, right was up, it was utter disaster and chaos, but yet it was normal. 4 months down from my 22nd birthday the call came through the radio waves, the war was ended on all fronts, for the first time in almost 25 years there was peace, for the first time in my life there was peace around me. All parties signed a peace deal a couple of days later. Except us, the generation born in war, moulded by it, made for it, there was no peace how could there be? We saw our best friends die by the grimy hands of war, forged friendships in battle based off of our mutual situation in war, from a young age we had family die from war, and all of a sudden the two certainties of our life, war and death, are no longer a certainty. Back home walking through the town I saw kids playing, little kids innocent still, likely to never be molested by war, on the swings and the slides. The military posts scattered throughout the town all but gone, any trace of the war slowly fading into the backdrop of history, soon to be taught to children as history rather than current affairs. But the war followed me, I couldn't adapt to the seeming normality around me because inside my conscious was blood stained and in tatters. Every little noise like a spoon dropping on the floor, or a door slamming too hard would startle me and shake me, yet these noises should be the noises of home. So what was this place with such foreign noises? It couldn't be home, no my home had the noise of attrition sirens, guns fizzling past your head, only to hit a comrade next to you. My life was death and now I must find a life in peace. For the first time in 6 years I slept in a bed surrounded by walls and insulation, comfortable, yet eerily too quiet. I awoke the next morning to find a brochure slipped under my door with the letters VSG printed on it. My reaction was to hide behind the wall and look through the blinds. The thought of someone at my door whilst I was sleeping shot anxiety through my body. Was this an ambush? Were they spies or scouts learning of our battle strength? Anxiety crept in as I waited for the attrition, I came to the conclusion that the enemy was scouting key positions for attrition, perhaps this brochure was a signal beacon of sorts. I came to my senses once my mum woke up. She found me under the table yelling at her to "get the Fuck down!" once I came to my senses I read the brochure, mum spoke to me about it. It was a group of people in the town, a mixture of veterans, psychologists and volunteers who have come together to help people like me live with what we have seen and experienced, the Veterans Support Group, the reason I am writing this, the reason I can pour my previous life of perpetual death onto a page. The reason I can find some form of peace with the war still raging on in my conscious.

In his book Humanism (1997), Tony Davies refers to these critics as "humanist anti-humanists." Antihumanists, particularly Jurgen Habermas, argue that although they point out the shortcomings of humanism in fulfilling its emancipatory goals, they do not propose their own alternative emancipatory projects. Some philosophers, such as Heidegger, identified with humanism in the spirit of the ancient Greeks but believed it was limited to the German "race" and specifically to the Nazis, leading Davies to call them "anti-humanist humanists." A critical interpretation of Heidegger's thoughts is itself highly debated; he includes his own perspectives and critiques of humanism in his Letter on Humanism. Davies recognizes that following the devastating events of the 20th-century wars, phrases like "the destiny of man" or "the triumph of human reason" must now carry an immediate awareness of their flawed and violent implications. He notes that it is nearly impossible to conceive of a crime that did not occur under the guise of human reason. However, he concludes that it would be unwise to entirely discard the legacy of historical humanisms. One reason for this is that humanism still offers the only viable alternative to prejudice and persecution in many instances. The freedom to express and articulate ideas, to organize and advocate for individual or group interests, and to challenge and resist authority—these principles can only be effectively communicated within the framework of humanism.

In this case, "black" is the absence of any light, and "white" is 100 of all other colors; color code: white or white and black means no lights. The following are some examples of color codes: RED: RED means no lights; RED indicates no lights; RED indicates only white. IBES: The colors red, orange, yellow, and green indicate no lights; orange represents no lights; yellow indicates no lights; orange signifies no lights. Red also signifies no lights in addition to white or orange. RED indicates that no lights exist. Color Code: RED denotes having NO lights. UVRED: The codes of blue, magenta, purple, cyan, yellow, and cyan represent no light except for those four variants (red half-light colors): red, orange, purple, green, and blue. These codes are not numeric representations but are represented by numbers indicating the brightness levels of the red filters used to specify what filtering scheme should be applied when determining whether a filter is needed or recommended. Yellow indicates no lights; yellow represents no lights. Orange indicates no lights except for those specified by the color codes above when using a white filter. Black indicates no lights unless a brightness level greater than 50 is prescribed for that filter. Chrome indicates a dark gray noise that does not produce an audible noise throughout the room due to light intake. Purple indicates no lights unless there are additional filters applied. Gold indicates no lights except white with no supplemental lighting such as lamps, LED lights on rooms 2 feet from ceiling height, and ceiling fans. Blue indicates no lights except when specified values exceed 50 of total illumination. Green indicates no lights except when specific filters apply. We examine the computational complexity of motion planning using local "input-output" gadgets with distinct entry and exit points, along with a subset of permissible traversal paths from entries to exits, each altering the state of the gadget and consequently the allowable traversals. We investigate such gadgets in the contexts of 0-, 1-, and 2-player scenarios, particularly expanding previous research on motion planning through gadgets to 0-player games for the first time by employing "branchless" connections between gadgets that direct all exits to a single entrance of another gadget. Our findings encompass containment within L, NL, P, NP, and PSPACE; as well as hardness for NL, P, NP, and PSPACE. These outcomes are applied to demonstrate PSPACE-completeness for specific mechanics in Factorio, [the Sequence], and a constrained variant of Trainyard, enhancing earlier results. This work reinforces prior conclusions regarding switching graphs and reachability switching games.

Myra Forde's ex-lawyer says she did not state that the late PM was a client, nor did she threaten to expose him if a prosecution against her was continued. Forde, a Sydney woman charged with sending a dozen letters to a number of politicians and high-profile media personalities including the prime minister and his then-chief of staff Peter Costello, made the comments on Thursday as part of a joint defence agreement with Forde's husband Peter. In court documents, Forde's lawyer said his client was only responding to a series of questions posed by the then-NSW Director of Public Prosecutions, Mike Le Mesurier, on May 23, 2012. "Myra Forde was asked, in reference to her communications with former Prime Minister, Mr Costello, whether she was aware that Mr Costello was a former client of Mr Le Mesurier," the documents read. "Myra Forde replied: 'No, I wasn't aware of that. I didn't know Mr Costello was a client of yours. I only learned that after you told me.' "Mr Le Mesurier then asked Myra Forde: 'You said you didn't know. But you were aware, correct?' "Myra Forde replied: 'Yes, I was aware.' "Mr Le Mesurier then asked Myra Forde: 'Did you threaten to expose Mr Costello if you were prosecuted?' "Myra Forde replied: 'No, I didn't. I'm not sure what you're getting at. I wasn't threatened.' "Mr Le Mesurier then asked Myra Forde: 'Do you deny you threatened to expose Mr Costello?' "Myra Forde replied: 'No, I don't deny that.' "Myra Forde also denied making any other statements that could be construed as threats to expose Mr Costello." On Friday, Forde's lawyer, Hugh Tomlinson, told the court the joint defence agreement did not provide that the information given by Forde would be used as evidence against her. "My client has not breached her plea of not guilty to any offence," Mr Tomlinson said. "The defence agreement was entered into with the knowledge of both parties that it would be used as evidence against Myra Forde in a trial of this matter." Mr Tomlinson said Forde had only responded to the questions put to her by Mr Le Mesurier. "My client has been truthful in all her responses," Mr Tomlinson said. "The defence agreement was entered into by Myra Forde and Mr Peter Forde in full knowledge that the defence agreement could be used as evidence against Myra Forde in a trial of this matter." Mr Tomlinson said the fact that Forde was charged in 2012 was "no surprise to Myra Forde." "Myra Forde is not surprised that the charges were brought against her," Mr Tomlinson said. "The Crown has the power to charge a person with an offence."

When you complete a credit card transaction, you inform the merchant that you wish to withdraw funds from your account and specify how much you're authorized to take. This process typically involves entering card details online or swiping the card at a terminal. Debit cards often require a PIN, whereas credit cards may ask for a zip code. At a gas station, you might enter your credit card information by inserting the card into a reader or typing in the required data. A criminal could position a device near the reader to steal your card details. These devices are often difficult to detect. For example, comparing an ATM with and without a secondary device to read the card as it's inserted shows this capability. The thief may then install a number pad reader or place a camera to monitor your input. Once they have the information, they can generate a new card using the stolen data and later use your card wherever it's accepted. There have been instances where someone at a gas station claims to need cash but offers to fill up your tank in return, using a stolen card and taking your money. It's important to note that you aren't being scammed; rather, the gas station loses the money if the card is reported stolen. Some credit cards, particularly those used in Europe, employ a "chip and pin" system, where a small computer chip on the card stores transaction details. When you make a payment, the card reader transmits the details along with your PIN to the chip, which then generates a unique authorization number for that specific transaction.

A group of researchers has developed a way to create food without sunlight using artificial photosynthesis. The method involves converting carbon dioxide, electricity, and water into acetate, and then feeding it to microbes that will create a biofuel. This biofuel can then be used for transportation or energy production. Artificial photosynthesis was initially proposed as a method of creating a low-carbon future. The process involves collecting solar energy and converting it into chemical energy using a solar power cell. This allows us to extract energy without relying on fossil fuels, which are a non-renewable resource. For the first time, researchers have shown that artificial photosynthesis can be used to produce food. The team from MIT and CMU has created a system that collects sunlight and converts it into chemical energy that can be used to create food. The team has also managed to create a prototype that can produce enough acetate to feed yeast. The system uses a solar power cell to collect light, as well as a catalyst that can convert electricity and carbon dioxide into acetate. The team then used this acetate to feed microbes, which in turn produced a biofuel. The process allows us to create a sustainable supply of food without using sunlight, which is the current limiting factor in the process. Solar power cells have improved over the years and it's possible that in the future we could have a system that collects sufficient light to support a food production system. It's not a question of whether or not artificial photosynthesis will ever be possible, but when.

Towcester racecourse chief executive Kevin Ackerman has failed in his bid to overturn a six-month suspension from racing. Ackerman was found guilty of breaching rules relating to the use of medication on two horses, and was given a suspended sentence last month. However, he appealed the decision and asked for a stay of execution so that he could continue to work while the appeal was heard. That request was rejected by the British Horseracing Authority (BHA), and Ackerman will now have to step down from his role at the Northamptonshire course. It is a blow for Towcester, which is due to host its first meeting of the season next week. Ackerman had been working hard to get the course ready for action after it was closed for several months due to financial problems. The BHA said it was "not appropriate" for Ackerman to remain in his post while the appeal was ongoing. Ackerman said he was "disappointed" with the decision and that he would be considering his options.

To extend battery life the phones have gone to lower voltages and more controlled power emissions. That has reduced the effective distance at which the average circuit can pick up an input, or cut-out current that's required to complete a circuit like this: A high voltage DC motor is used to push a wire into the starter switch on your car and it spins its spindles to spin the starter solenoid. The capacitor in combination with the high voltage switch prevents the starter from flicking open when the battery is fully charged (hence 'relay starter. Without a starter (or if you're lucky enough to own one), you would need to disconnect the wires from the ignition system, remove the relay (s) from their sockets, replace the starter solenoid, put the new solenoid in place of the old switch (and a separate fusible link fuse for Safety), then reconnect everything again minus the wires connecting the starter solenoid to the ignition coil and minus the fuses above for safety reasons. This takes about five minutes per vehicle. If you were to just use the standard AC DC battery charger, you could do it in less than three minutes - because you don't have the relays, the capacitor, the Fuse Blocker and all those pesky connections between inductors, capacitors, resistors etc...! So let me get this straight, we have a problem with our vehicles starting on empty, yet they won't start without batteries? Time to upgrade them to lithium ion batteries! Oh wait, cars don't run off lithium ions anymore; they run off electrons. So we'll stick with electric motors and generators until our cars become self-driving.

The personal copying exemption under EU copyright legislation originates from the 2001 EU Copyright Directive, which permits member states to establish rules governing unauthorized copying for personal, non-commercial purposes. The directive did not aim to endorse file sharing but instead addressed the practice of redistributing copyrighted material from legally acquired CDs to specific devices and media, provided rights holders receive compensation and copy protection mechanisms are not bypassed. Compensation methods vary by country and typically involve levies on recording equipment and media or taxes on the content itself. In some nations, such as Canada, there have been ongoing discussions regarding the application of these laws to copying onto general-purpose storage mediums like hard drives, portable media players, and mobile phones, where no levies are imposed.

My phone rang a fourth time that day, and I rushed to check it, eager to see if it was a follow-up call from the job I had applied for. My current position wasn't satisfying, and my finances were tight. This editing role wasn't the dream, but if I secured the opportunity, I could at least maintain a basic standard of living. Clearly, it wasn't. It was merely an email alert, another of those relentless spam messages urging me to "JOIN THE ILLUMANITI TODAY! WE NEED YOU." God damn it, that must have been the thousandth such message I've received in the past month, and it's been ongoing for a while now. No matter how hard I tried to block them, the emails kept returning. Adding them to the spam filter didn't help; they began coming from different email addresses the next day, and by the following day, they were back again. Blocking them with another app or ad blocker didn't work either. Even after deleting my email app, I still received notifications from other sources. Facebook, YouTube, and even Reddit started sending me inbox messages. I didn't take it seriously at first—just some guy doing an over-the-top joke. There was a fictional writing site I frequently visited, where I often participated in the sci-fi section, collaborating with a friend on dystopian stories. I always took the lead in structuring these societies and their actions. We had a great time, and our readers provided some decent feedback. I hadn't expected any negative repercussions. The emails started appearing when we discussed a world where the Illuminati controlled everything. Naturally, I ignored them, assuming it was just my friend playing a prank. However, as the emails continued, I confronted him, and it became evident he had no idea what I was referring to. So it wasn't him, but it could have easily been someone else from that site. This notification came through Facebook, so I decided to remove it from my phone. It was becoming increasingly frustrating. I barely finished moving through the list.

We present a bandit algorithm, SAO (Stochastic and Adversarial Optimal), whose regret is, essentially, optimal both for adversarial rewards and for stochastic rewards. Specifically, SAO combines the O (n) worst-case regret of Exp3 [, ] for adversarial rewards and the (poly) logarithmic regret of UCB1 [, ] for stochastic rewards. Adversarial rewards and stochastic rewards are the two main settings in the literature on (non-Bayesian) multi-armed bandits. Prior work on multi-armed bandits treats them separately, and does not attempt to jointly optimize for both. Our result falls into a general theme of achieving good worst-case performance while also taking advantage of "nice" problem instances, an important issue in the design of algorithms with partially known inputs.

Ministers are to increase the maximum discount - currently PS16,000 to PS38,000 - to more than the expected PS50,000. They hope it will persuade more tenants and mortgage lenders to get involved in the scheme first started in the 1980s. But housing charity Shelter says the plans risk diminishing the stock of "genuinely affordable" social housing. It also says the plans could saddle low-income families with mortgage debts they cannot afford. The "right to buy" scheme was first started under Margaret Thatcher's government. In December the government launched a consultation on "re-invigorating" the right to buy, which has dwindled in recent years, and suggested the maximum discount may be raised to PS50,000. Currently, discount levels differ across the country, ranging from PS16,000 to PS38,000. Now ministers believe discounts should be as high as PS75,000, the BBC understands. The government insists all social homes that are sold "will be replaced on a one-for-one basis by a new affordable rent property, ensuring there is no reduction in the number of affordable homes." But Shelter says it will still have the effect of damaging social housing. Roger Harding, Shelter's head of policy, research and public affairs, said: "The government is not going to replace like-with-like. "The'affordable rent' model means landlords can charge rents of up to 80 of market rates, which is typically higher than council rents. "The net result will be a reduction in the number of genuinely affordable homes for families on modest incomes." He added: "That could have the added effect of pushing up the housing benefit bill, if there are fewer council houses and more'affordable rent' properties with higher rental costs." Mr Harding said: "We are also concerned that ownership is not necessarily the most financially suitable form of tenure for a lot of social housing tenants. "Many are on very low incomes and could find themselves unable to afford the mortgage repayments. Statistically, right-to-buy mortgage holders are far more likely than other purchasers to have their homes repossessed." Later this week Housing Minister Grant Shapps is expected to say: "This coalition government backs the dreams of those who want to own the roof over their own head." He has promised to triple or even quadruple the discounts available to "hard-working families." Mr Shapps will say: "New home buyers will have the satisfaction of knowing that for each property sold, we'll be aiming to replace it with a new affordable home for the record numbers left languishing on Labour's housing waiting lists. "It's a winwin that backs aspirational council tenants whilst dealing with the legacy of Labour's record waiting lists."

Today will be a good day. It's a flight from LaGuardia to LAX, like any other. Weather is good, and it's my last flight before vacation starts. My name is Captain Dustin Phillips, and I am a 20-year veteran of United Airlines. We fly to and from every airport, and I fly every airplane. There isn't one bird that I can't get into the head of and tell it what to do. Speaking of getting into something's head, I need to take my medicine. I am bi-polar and schizophrenic. It's my darkest secret, and I wouldn't have a set of wings if anyone knew. I pay top dollar for a doctor to manage my illness and keep his mouth closed; and my wife is a pharmacist, so my medicinal needs are well met. I go into the bathroom, and that's when it hits me. I don't have my medication. I search every pocket..... nothing. The thoughts that pass through my head at a mile a minute scare the living hell out of me. Imagine murdering a person and waiting for the police to arrest you, the guilt overwhelming you as you come to realize the brevity of what you've done. I am realizing the brevity of my mistake, and I can't believe how irresponsible I am. I am terrified of all the things that I think when I'm left to my natural devices. I am more than Captain Dustin Phillips..... I am God. I am a being beyond reproach, judgmental and omniscient. I know all things, and I can easily justify doing just about anything, because I tell myself that it is the right thing. I have to stop thinking about it. It should only be about 36 hours until I get home, which leaves 60 hours without it. I will be fine. I have to be. I prepare my uniform; I grab lunch and a cup of coffee. I go through my motions; routine is the basis for sanity, right? I smile, and conceal the worry. It's impossible not to worry. I know what comes of this. "Hey man, how are you feeling?" I turn and see my co-pilot. "Allen. I'm good. Really good. " I give a smirk and we board the plane. I know the moment I lost my sanity. I looked at the overweight man, the man who will have a hard time without his child pornography. The teenage lovers, who think that today, will be the day they join the Mile High Club. The soldier who kills for a living and the woman who is more worried about her makeup than consoling her son, who is quite obviously terrified. His faith is weak. There is a baby, an unholy screaming baby. I hate babies. I have a seat in the cockpit, and start going through my checks. I've done this a million times before, so no need to be particular. I can do anything, right? "Are the passengers boarded?" "Yes sir, are you ready for your walk around?" "Sure." I walked around the plane, not really looking for anything. We shifted the plane into gear, taxied on the runway and positioned ourselves for takeoff. My phone rings. It's my wife. "Dustin, please tell me you're not flying. Please tell me you're taking off sick. Honey, please don't do this." "I'm fine darling." "Dustin, you're not fine. Don't you do this. Don't you leave me." "I love you, I'll be home tomorrow, I promise." "No, you can't do this, you can'...." I hung up. The feeling I got from her tearful begging, her honestly scared voice, with shaking that I almost never here. She really has no faith in me. The Bible tells her..... no, I told her, as every woman before her; trust and obey. Disobedient harlot. She should..... no, she will pay; when the day comes that she finally meets me. "You'd think that by now she'd be done being scared. " says my co-pilot. "Women. Sometimes I think she'd be better off medicated." The irony. I get a text. It's my wife. We begin takeoff, as I address the audience over the intercom. "Don't get lost in heaven. I love you." The radio squawks in the passenger cab. "I have seen your future, and it is a waste of humanity. Judgment day is nigh, and soon you shall all see the light. I am God, Yahweh, Allah..... call me what you want, but I can take your lives as easy as I created them. No need to pray, simply yell through the cockpit door. Enjoy your last flight." The co-pilot looks over in shock. The pilot simply smiles, as he reaches into his pocket to pull out the knife he kept with him, just in case he ever forgot his medication and needed to stop just such a disaster. His proverbial cyanide pill. The only problem is that crazy doesn't have a gray area, either you are or you aren't. By the time you realize that you've lost it, you're not sane enough get it back. Not even for a second. He stabs the co-pilot, who is much smaller than him, and he dies without as much as a struggle. The plane gradually ascends, the screams of the damned barely pervading the cockpit door. The stewardesses scream and pound on the door. Air traffic control is going nuts, and I climb. I climb and I climb and I climb. I can feel the sun enveloping me, and I can see the angels summoning me. I know what awaits and I am ready. The gates are open and I am cleared for landing. I hear a sputter and the engines shut off. Gauges and lights go crazy and the plane goes nose down. What is happening? I thought I was destined for this, and then I fall. I fall and fall and fall towards the flames below. The devil is smiling, and it is at this moment that I realize that I was never God. I was never anything but what I am. I can see the news headlines now, and I can't recover. I'm stalled and burning. There is no way to save the plane or its passengers. I begin to pray. As we near the ground, I remember the text message I received from my wife. I open it. "Don't get lost in heaven." I text back, "I love you, and I'm sorry." I enter the lake of fire, never to be seen again. The souls screaming in pain and agony are enough, and I close my eyes.

The world just wasn't the same once he was gone. In fact, most educated folk these days would say his death was the reason everything went so badly down hill, from the Civil War to the beginning of the Great Depression. The whole world was a different place, and when he died, it seemed like nothing was ever going to be the same again. When it was announced, the word spread like wildfire that the President of the United States had died. The nation was shocked. After all, he was the "Gipper" as he was called. The man who had overcome polio to become one of the most beloved presidents in the nation's history. Everyone in the country felt the loss of their beloved President. For some it was the end of an era, for others it was the end of hope. When the news reached my sister, she was in shock. She just sat there on the couch staring at the TV, she was like a zombie, her mind couldn't comprehend what was happening. It was like no one knew what to do. For a moment, everyone seemed to be in a state of shock. All the sudden, people were weeping and crying, and asking, "What will happen now?" No one could answer. I can't even explain how my sister felt. After all, she wasn't even sure if she felt anything. She was numb, as if her life had suddenly come to a screeching halt. She didn't know what to do, or how to react, or what to say. In fact, she didn't even know how to feel. For a long time, she sat there, staring at the television, crying softly. She was sad, and alone. She didn't feel like doing anything, and she didn't know what to do. I'll never forget that day. It was the saddest day of my life. I never saw her so upset. It was as if all the joy and happiness she had ever felt had been sucked out of her. It was so weird, but I felt like I was going to be sick, like I was dying. I kept wondering, "Why did this have to happen? Why did it have to be him? Why did it have to be the Gipper?" I didn't know what to do or where to go. I didn't know what to say or how to react. For a moment, I felt as if I were in a nightmare, and I couldn't wake up. Then, my eyes lit up. "I know what I can do." I thought to myself. I went to the kitchen and grabbed a butter knife. I went to the living room and sat next to my sister. "I'll be back," I said as I walked out the door. I was gone for about 15 minutes. When I came back, my sister had tears streaming down her face. In modern operating systems, such as Linux distributions and Windows 7/8, users typically have two types of permissions. Your regular user account allows you to make changes to your computer, like installing programs or adjusting settings. However, this account has limited privileges; you can mess with things, but only affect your own account. Others using the same computer are protected from your errors and continue without issue.

The other type of user has greater power. On Windows, this is often referred to as a "system administrator." If you can log in as a system administrator, you gain almost god-like control—capable of breaking the system down through reckless actions. In Linux, the equivalent is "root," a term that signifies absolute authority. Just like a Windows admin, the "root" user has unrestricted power upon logging in.

The key difference is that normally, when connecting to a remote Linux server, you use a non-root user account to log in. To perform administrative tasks, you switch to the root account using the "su" command.

Event-specific concepts are the semantic concepts specifically designed for the events of interest, which can be used as a mid-level representation of complex events in videos. Existing methods only focus on extracting event-specific concepts from videos, but cannot learn visual representations for them. Recent research has used deep learning techniques to learn visual representations of event-specific concepts from videos. For example, researchers have applied convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn visual representations of event-specific concepts from videos. CNNs can be trained to recognize specific objects or activities in the video and then used to extract event-specific features. Additionally, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) have been used to learn temporal relationships between events in videos and extract event-specific concepts. RNNs are particularly useful for analyzing long sequences of video frames and recognizing complex events. Other deep learning methods such as autoencoders and variational autoencoders (VAEs) have also been employed to learn visual representations of event-specific concepts from videos. In conclusion, deep learning techniques such as CNNs, RNNs, autoencoders, and VAEs can be used to learn visual representations of event-specific concepts from videos. These methods allow us to extract high-level semantic information from videos, which can be used to better understand complex events in videos.

Binary neural network classifiers are typically assessed using metrics such as accuracy and F 1 -Score, which rely on confusion matrix values—such as true positives, false positives, false negatives, and true negatives. However, these classifiers are usually trained with a distinct loss function, for example, log loss. It is generally more favorable to use the same loss during training as the evaluation metric, but this proves challenging when working with confusion matrix-based metrics due to the nature of set membership, which is a step function lacking a derivative suitable for backpropagation. To tackle this issue, we introduce an approximation of the step function that satisfies the requirements for efficient training of binary neural networks using confusion matrix-based metrics. This method enables end-to-end training of binary deep neural classifiers through batch gradient descent. We illustrate the versatility of this approach across various applications involving differing degrees of class imbalance. Additionally, we show how the approximation facilitates a balanced trade-off between precision and recall depending on the specific task needs.

Given the widespread application of embeddings as input representations in numerous natural language tasks, addressing the challenge of imputing embeddings for rare and unseen words is crucial in language processing. Embedding imputation entails learning representations for such words during the training phase of an embedding model, usually implemented post-training. In this study, we introduce a method for embedding imputation that leverages grounded information through a knowledge graph. This contrasts with prior techniques that rely on vector space characteristics or subword data. Our approach employs an online strategy to generate a graph based on grounded information and develops an algorithm to transform the resulting graph into the space of pre-trained embeddings. We assess our method on diverse tasks involving rare and unseen words and demonstrate its effectiveness. For instance, on the Card-660 dataset, our method enhances Pearson’s and Spearman’s correlation coefficients by 11 and 17.8 relative to the state-of-the-art using GloVe embeddings. Prosecuting, Paul Eales QC, said: "Jessica Taylor was suffering from Chronic Fatigue Syndrome and felt she was unable to keep up with Bearman. "He offered to take her out for dinner in his car. They drove around for an hour, but were unable to go further because she was so unwell." Bearman drove Miss Taylor to her home in London's Wandsworth where he left her to go to a nightclub with a friend. When he returned he called Miss Taylor and asked her to come to his home. "He wanted to show her a photo of his friend's baby," Mr Eales said. "When she arrived he was in his underwear and she had to stay with him in the room while he showered. "When he came out she asked him to leave and he did so. "But she had sex with him in his car later that evening." Mr Eales said the couple continued to have sex over the next few weeks before Miss Taylor became ill and had to cancel a date with Bearman. "She said she was in a constant state of exhaustion, her muscles were very painful and she had constant headaches. "She had no energy and her work suffered." Primary resistance arises when an individual contracts a resistant strain of tuberculosis. A person with susceptible Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) might develop secondary (acquired) resistance during treatment due to insufficient medication, improper adherence to the prescribed regimen, or the use of substandard drugs. Drug-resistant tuberculosis is a significant public health concern in many developing nations, as it necessitates longer treatment durations and more costly medications. Multidrug-resistant (MDR)-TB is characterized by resistance to the two most effective initial treatment drugs, rifampicin and isoniazid. Extensively drug-resistant (XDR)-TB is additionally resistant to three or more of the six categories of second-line drugs. Fully drug-resistant TB shows resistance to all currently available medications. This form of resistance was initially identified in Italy in 2003 but gained wider recognition in 2012 and has also been documented in Iran and India. Bedaquiline is being considered for the treatment of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis.

Rye. Again. The picnic table bench creaked as I shifted from thigh to thigh. The boxed lunch I had pilfered from the office break room, leftover from some unfortunate souls who were bribed by free food to attend a lunchtime seminar on "The Eight Time Saving Rules and You," was once again unsatisfactory. A vegetable sandwich on rye bread with a pickle in a Ziploc bag and what appeared to be a digestive biscuit. Beggars can't be choosers though. It had been three days since I left the office. The long range plan was due tomorrow, and for a guy in finance, that meant staying all night. You did what you needed to do to get the job done, and with layoffs around the corner, everyone was out for themselves. My database access had just been revoked due to someone looking at the server the wrong way, so free lunch and freer sunshine beckoned. Chewing thoughtfully, I tried to focus on where I was, the present moment. Anything to escape my churning brain. Closing my eyes, I could hear birds twittering away, staccatic shouts of children at the playground, bicycles winding around the pathways. The rye bread got soggier in my mouth, and a bitter rancid taste took over from the dry bready flavor. I realized that this sandwhich might not have been from that day's lunch seminar, but possibly from last week's monthly lunch and learn Legal Hold Orders: What do do, Who to Contact. I opened my eyes and looked at the half sandwich remaining and sighed. I put a hand to my stomach, hoping I wouldn't pay for this meal later. I rested my arms on the table and rested my head on my arms. "Hey, pal, can you spare a few crumbs?" I must have fallen asleep as this gentleman's voice woke me up. I raised my head and mumbled "ts gone bad, bub..." as I looked into the face of an inquisitive pigeon sitting on the table a foot from my face. I blinked at the bird. It blinked back at me. I slowly pushed the rancid veggie sandwich over towards it. It pecked at it hesitantly, cooed, and fluttered off to the nearest tree. I handed in my resignation at 2 PM.

The Electronic Design Automation (EDA) sector extensively employs third-party Intellectual Property (IP) cores. These cores are susceptible to the injection of Hardware Trojans (HTs) during the design phase, either by third-party IP providers or by malicious insiders within the design team. Current HT detection methods, which assert they can identify all publicly available HT benchmarks, are increasingly compromised by the creation of advanced and complex HTs. This occurs because such techniques restrict their analysis to public HT benchmarks or simpler variants. However, adversaries are not confined to these types of HTs and may develop novel design strategies to circumvent these defenses. In this study, we uncover key characteristics of HTs that enable the definition of an exponentially vast class of Deterministic Hardware Trojans (HD), which an adversary can create but is not restricted to. These insights form the basis of HT design principles, enabling the development of a new HT named XOR-LFSR, presented as a proof-of-concept example from the HD class. These principles facilitate a deeper understanding of how adversaries might design HTs and demonstrate that the existing publicly known HT benchmarks represent merely a fraction of the broader landscape. Consequently, this work underscores the need for robust HT detection tools that account for newly identified design principles, ensuring the identification of an exponentially large number of HTs—those with a negligible false negative rate—regardless of the size of the IP core's wire count.

The group lost its support following the 2005 assassination of Morsi, who was overthrown by military dictator Mozhgidi. Last month, AQIM attacked the mosque in Alexandria using ammonium nitrate propellant detonators causing more than 100 deaths including two journalists. The rotating armature consists of one or more coils of wire wound around a laminated, magnetically "soft" ferromagnetic core. Current from the brushes flows through the commutator and one winding of the armature, making it a temporary magnet (an electromagnet). The magnetic field produced by the armature interacts with a stationary magnetic field produced by either PMs or another winding a field coil, as part of the motor frame. The force between the two magnetic fields tends to rotate the motor shaft. The commutator switches power to the coils as the rotor turns, keeping the magnetic poles of the rotor from ever fully aligning with the magnetic poles of the stator field, so that the rotor never stops (like a compass needle does), but rather keeps rotating as long as power is applied.

I sometimes venture into the woods to unwind. The quiet is soothing, but only briefly. When I pause and listen, I soon realize how noisy nature truly is. A chorus of birds, insects, and creatures all chatter and screech within the trees, swaying and creaking in the breeze. It's a cacophony. However, one day everything changed. As I approached, the birds and insects became silent. I wouldn't have paused unless I had unexpectedly stumbled upon a strange, empty area where no chirps, whistles, cries, or calls were audible. Instead, there was a low, relentless scream. It didn’t sound like a scream right away—it was more of an odd hum, slightly high-pitched, varying in tone, pitch, and volume. I stopped, gaping in disbelief, uncertain whether I was hearing something real. I stretched my jaw and tried to pop my ears as if experiencing tinnitus, but nothing changed. I turned around, convinced there might be a power plant nearby, but all I saw was the opening. It was about a foot wide, perfectly circular, yet old enough that the edges were worn and eroded. The hum grew louder, and as I lowered my head, I felt an unsettling sense that it echoed like screaming. Yet it wasn’t from an animal or human—something else entirely. My body tensed, my heart racing, my vision trembling as the intensity of the sound made me feel like I was being watched. I pushed myself away, stumbling back, falling down, and moving slowly away through the foliage and fallen logs, desperate to escape this enigmatic hole. After a moment of breathing deeply, I regained my composure, standing up and wiping the leaves from my clothes. I exhaled slowly and reminded myself that there must be an explanation, that there’s no way such a phenomenon could exist in such vast numbers.

One of the more notable applications of printing technology was the chao, the paper money of the Yuan. Chao were made from the bark of mulberry trees. The Yuan government with this paper money was not only used to pay for products and services which had been supplied by the Yuan merchants but also for education purposes such as textbooks and medical supplies without any foreign currency. In April 1953, the Yuan government allocated a total of 50 billion Yuan for printing business enterprises in order to the printing press companies to supply government institutions, schools, hospitals etc. These funds could be spent on numerous other things affecting its economy according to government regulations. In 1957 the Yuan government decided to use Yuan money to fund institutions establishing factories or institutes, including the banks and public hospitals. The Yuan government set up printing presses at a cost of US100 million per year while printing presses operated at lower costs than those at China International Printing Press Limited (CIPP). During the 1950s central bank printing guidelines prohibited printing press owners from using Yuan money to buy goods produced outside China until 1958. In 1962 printing operations ceased after China's military came into being under the control of the military regime. China's printing presses have since expanded dramatically thanks mainly to printing presses bought overpaid by the military and private developers who managed them independently from the state sector firms. For example, in January 1961 printing presses were purchased by the Ministry of Education for US 1,000 each plus postage paid for printing presses printed in China. This printing presses are still in operation today. The Chinese currency has changed hands several times during the past century - it peaked at yuan denominated in US dollars between 1949 and 1967 when it started trading at nearly US15 and went down again towards US10 before bouncing back upwards thereafter due to China's economic growth in the 1970s. Since then, however, central bankers have repeatedly expressed concern that Beijing is moving away from using Yuan values because they believe the exchange rate will overturn the monetary system and cause distortions in investments based on the value of Yuan appreciation compared to dollarization rates. Russian Central Bank Governor Igor Ivanov recently alluded to this issue saying the volume of Yuan dollars imported out of Russia plummeted to two trillion roubles (357 billion) annually beginning in 2012-2013 amid concerns about inflation pressures and negative interest rates imposed by its powerful ruler Vladimir Putin. Ivanov pointed out that the lack of liquidity means that investors can no longer make purchases cheaply abroad despite pressure from the export industry to keep yuan prices stable. Once the yuan devaluation becomes too aggressive, Ivanov warned that the current situation risks triggering deflationary consequences like the current crisis caused by China recession. There exists a general perception among investors that the Yuan should be run domestically rather than relying entirely on foreign lenders. However, the fundamentals remain sound enough that China simply cannot become dependent solely upon external sources unless countries acknowledge their intentions and seek corrective measures through agreement with national governments and businesses involved in the printing process. China needs to put some effort into ensuring stability across its real estate market where loans provided by foreign creditors are nonrefundable eventually leading to considerable uncertainty resulting in damage to property investment opportunities instead of boosting demand and attracting investors who would otherwise invest elsewhere if there weren't risk aversion. Conclusion: The Chinese economy continues evolving rapidly which may lose momentum quickly once the new generation of young population arrives in China, as people forget about the past problems associated with the Yuan currency. China remains reliant on exports driven mostly by foreign capital inflows although most export revenues come directly from deposits recovered by national banks following the 2008 financial crisis as well as from imports. Economic reforms must clearly intervene so that decisions taken during the initial stages of resurgence don't exacerbate hardships experienced earlier in the 1990's when the Yuan became weaker relative to other peer currencies weakened reserves exacerbated by external shocks. China urgently requires authorities to take action against corruption especially given the huge loopholes left open by the collapse of the Yuan banking system. More importantly, China strongly believes that pursuing reforms pursued jointly won't solve the problem created by the current weakening of Yuan values even though external factors influence its actions accordingly.

Businesses set up shop next to a rival for two reasons. The first is because they want to be close to their customers. If their customers are already going to a rival business, it makes sense to set up shop nearby so that they can get some of those customers. The second reason is because businesses want to be close to their suppliers. If their suppliers are already located near a rival business, it makes sense to set up shop nearby so that they can get cheaper supplies.

It worked. By all the gods, somehow it had worked. Dunstan gazed wearily from the precipice of the crumbling tower. Empty, battered armor and sharpened steel lay in all directions, robbed of their purpose and the promises of soft flesh to tear through. A bitter wind gnawed on the empty battlefield, not a drop of blood or scrap of flesh stained the land other than his own, and that of the figure rising from the thickest hill of plate and chain mail. Even dear, sweet Roman who until a moment ago had been bleeding out in Dunstan's arms, was no more but his empty robes. To call it an invasion would have been a cruel joke. The northern forces had outnumbered the small watchtower many thousands to one. It hadn't been a question of if the tower would fall, but how many minutes they could buy until it did, and if they would be tortured before they died. They were, in many cases literally, already dead. Dunstan hadn't had any other choice..... "You are he who summoned me then?" growled a voice like the grinding wheels of a trebuchet. It hadn't been a question, so much as an acknowledgement. Dunstan swiveled his head, meekly fixing his gaze on the statuesque figure, now joining him at the top of the tower. His pristine, white suit was of a cut that the mage had never seen. A god, one whose true name had been lost to the ages, one of war and commerce, loomed above him. His fierce visage blocked out the sun like a thunderstorm. Dunstan nodded meekly. Much of his own blood had been lost in the exchange, but compared to the thousands now gone, he could hardly allow himself to complain. "What do I call you?" he asked, rising to his feet. The man-beast grasped the empty robes at Dunstan's feet, as though reading something in its very threading. "You may call me Roman," he sneered. His teeth were like ivory, and so sharp that even gazing at the edge of them felt like a paper-cut on Dunstan's eyes. "Now..... where is my war I'd been promised?" "There isn't any. You ended it..... Roman." The mage winced at the desecration of his best friend and comrade's name, "We were but a small fort, made an example of with the sheer number of the northern bandits' forces. I paid the price of summoning you with the flesh, blood and bone of the entire battlefield. We won. The northern bandits are no more. You may leave now, Roman. You have my thanks." Dunstan had expected the god's smirk to fall, to twist into a scowl, but it only broadened, showing yet more rows of sharpened teeth. "Oh no, no, my little wizard friend. That's not how this works," Roman cackled, his laugh like the delighted caw of a thousand battlefield crows, "There will be war. I will not leave until I have my war. I will drink my fill of blood, soldier and peasant alike. I will feast upon a generation yet. And you, you my wizardly friend, will guzzle deeply upon the glory of the victorious general. Such is the contract, and so it shall be." Panic willed Dunstan's broken body into alertness. He filled with a manic energy only the truly terrified ever know. "N-No!" he protested, "We can't! The northern bandits are no more. We took their lord, he lays amongst the sacrificed. There is no more war to be had here!" Dunstan reached to grasp Roman's lapel, to gain some kind of hold on the god, but his fingertips snatched only at air. Another cackle shook the battered tower. "No more war? My foolish friend, surely you jest. Have they no homeland? Have they no allies? Have they no family? If there is truly no more war to be had, worry not, wizard. War is easily made." From every seam in Roman's spotless white tuxedo, dark, stale blood poured, staining his suit nearly jet black if not for the gleam of crimson. The poisoned blood etched the cracks in the stone floor, flowing like a fountain down the tower, seeping into the torn landscape below. It pooled in the armor of the fallen, filling each slowly. In every direction, armor rose, suits filling with the new flesh of faceless figures. The sound of marching echoed through the hills as the strangers departed in every direction. "W-What are those things? Where are they going?" Dunstan again tried to grasp the god's suit, his hands staining with the thick, sludge-like blood. "Answer me, Roman!" he cried in desperation. "Those? Assassins. Saboteurs. Warlords. Politicians.'Misunderstandings' taken just a bit too far. Anyone who might be in just the wrong place at just the wrong time. Heroes. Villains. There are so many ways to start a war. Almost any excuse will do, really." Roman smiled. He looked upon the departing beasts as a doting mother might. "Many will return with armies for you to lead, as I promised you." "Why? Why must this happen, Roman? The price was paid already! Please, by the gods, leave this place and let the horrors end, unfathomable as they already are. Must I pay more, that you might leave? Must I throw myself from this tower to pay your toll?" Roman wrapped an arm around Dunstan as solid as stone, the thick blood rolling down his robes, bloodying them as badly as the previous ' Roman'had. "You thought the soldiers were my toll? Most of them weren't even yours to give, friend. No, no, war is the price that must be paid. This is why the world tried to forget me, why my true name was lost. Throw yourself, if you so wish. You may even find some courage in your plummet, but you will not find death. Dunstan, my friend, you will pay me my war, and in return I will garb you in riches and glory bought in blood. Such is the contract, so it shall be."

Everyone cherished Christmas, especially the residents of Groot. They admired the decorations, the ornaments, and the gifts. It was such a joyous occasion! They decorated the trees and hung the lights. Christmas was near, only seven nights away! The stores were full of shoppers, everyone buying presents. Some parents left their children in the elevators. People sang songs, and some kissed each other. Nobody saw the children vanish. Three nights before Christmas, the children came back. They sang new songs that they had learned. These weren't happy, not cheerful, or merry—they were sad, long, and serious. They were quite unpleasant to hear. On the night before Christmas, throughout Groot, there was a song that sounded worrying, as if something was wrong. The sky split open, so did the earth. There was no more Christmas without Cthulhu nearby.
